options: Since
Once
Although
Provided that
Whenever
questions.explanation: Politikaların büyük kamu yatırımı gerektirmesi ile yine de çok daha az maliyetli olması arasında bir zıtlık vardır; bunu 'although' (-e rağmen) karşılar. 'Since' neden, 'once' ve 'whenever' zaman, 'provided that' koşul bildirdiği için anlamı bozar.

questions.text: Although the ruins had been known to local villagers for centuries, ----.
options: they were frequently visited by travellers and merchants
the villagers had used stones from them to build their houses
because nobody had ever written about them in detail
so they were protected by strict laws from an early date
they were not systematically studied until the 1920s
questions.explanation: 'Although' zıtlık gerektirir: Kalıntılar yüzyıllardır biliniyordu, ama ancak 1920'lerde sistemli olarak incelendi. Ziyaret edilmeleri ya da taşlarının kullanılması bir zıtlık oluşturmaz; 'because' ve 'so' ile başlayan seçenekler ise 'although' ile aynı cümlede dil bilgisi açısından kullanılamaz.

questions.text: Had the central bank not lowered interest rates so sharply, ----.
options: the housing bubble might never have formed
investors will rush to buy more property
many families had bought homes they could not afford
the economy grows more slowly than expected
property prices rose dramatically in the following years
questions.explanation: 'Had ... not lowered' devrik yapısı 'If the central bank had not lowered' anlamında üçüncü tip koşul cümlesidir; sonuç kısmında 'might/would have + V3' gelir: 'the housing bubble might never have formed' (konut balonu hiç oluşmayabilirdi). Diğer seçeneklerdeki 'will rush', 'had bought', 'grows' ve 'rose' bu koşul yapısıyla uyumlu değildir.

questions.text: The new museum was designed with large glass walls ----.
options: even though it attracted thousands of visitors
so that natural light could illuminate the exhibits during the day
unless the collection had been moved elsewhere
whereas the architect had won several awards for his earlier projects abroad
as if the building were made entirely of stone
questions.explanation: Büyük cam duvarların amacı gün ışığının sergileri aydınlatmasıdır; amaç bildiren 'so that' (-sın diye) mantıklı bir bütün oluşturur. 'Even though' ve 'whereas' anlamsız bir zıtlık kurar, 'unless' koşulu cümleye uymaz, 'as if ... stone' ise cam duvarlarla çelişir.

questions.text: Just as the printing press transformed the way knowledge was shared in early modern Europe, ----.
options: many manuscripts were still copied by hand
although books remained expensive for most people
the internet has fundamentally changed how information circulates today
it was invented by Johannes Gutenberg in Germany around the middle of the fifteenth century
but few people could read at that time
questions.explanation: 'Just as' (tıpkı ... gibi) iki benzer durumu karşılaştırır: matbaa bilgi paylaşımını nasıl dönüştürdüyse internet de bilginin dolaşımını öyle değiştirmiştir. El yazmalarının kopyalanması ve icat tarihi bir benzerlik kurmaz; 'although' ve 'but' ile başlayan seçenekler ise yapıya dil bilgisi açısından uymaz.

questions.text: Sociologists have found that people who move to large cities often feel more isolated ----.
options: so that they can make new friends more easily
unless they had moved there in childhood
as soon as they have found a well-paid job
than they did in their home villages, despite being surrounded by more people
whereas city life offers them no opportunities at all to meet people from their own region
questions.explanation: 'More isolated' (daha yalnız) karşılaştırma yapısı 'than' ile tamamlanır: İnsanlar kalabalıklar içinde olmalarına rağmen kentte köylerinde olduğundan daha yalnız hisseder. 'So that' amacı mantıksızdır, 'unless' ve 'as soon as' zaman/koşul uyumsuzluğu yaratır, 'whereas' seçeneği ise abartılı ve ilgisiz bir zıtlık kurar.

questions.text: ----, the government decided to build a new capital city in the centre of the country.
options: Even though the coastal region had become overcrowded
Unless the population of the old capital continues to grow at its current rate
As long as the new city had not been planned
Before the old capital was even founded
In order to reduce the dominance of the overcrowded coastal region
questions.explanation: Yeni başkent kurma kararının amacı aşırı kalabalık kıyı bölgesinin baskınlığını azaltmaktır; 'in order to' (-mek amacıyla) bu ilişkiyi doğru kurar. Kalabalık bir neden olduğu için 'even though' ile zıtlık kurulamaz; 'unless' ve 'as long as' koşulları zaman uyumu açısından hatalıdır, eski başkent kurulmadan önce yeni başkent kurulması ise mantıksızdır.

questions.text: Renaissance artists studied ancient Roman sculpture closely, ----.
options: which helped them depict the human body with greater realism
although they had never shown any interest in the classical past
so they abandoned the idea of realistic human figures
unless they were working for wealthy patrons
whose works were later destroyed by the Romans
questions.explanation: 'Which' burada önceki cümlenin tamamını niteler: Roma heykellerini incelemek sanatçıların insan bedenini daha gerçekçi çizmesine yardım etti. Klasik geçmişe ilgi duymadıkları iddiası cümleyle çelişir, gerçekçiliği bırakmaları mantıksızdır; 'unless' koşulu ilgisizdir, Rönesans eserlerinin Romalılarca yok edilmesi ise kronolojik olarak imkânsızdır.

questions.text: Unemployment in the region remained high for decades ----.
options: since new industries quickly replaced the old ones and created thousands of new jobs
after the closure of the coal mines that had once employed most of its workers
so that wages would rise steadily
even though most of the mines had been closed
unless the government will invest in new industries
questions.explanation: İşsizliğin on yıllarca yüksek kalması, işçilerin çoğunu istihdam eden kömür madenlerinin kapanmasının ardından gerçekleşmiştir; 'after' bu neden-sonuç ilişkisini doğru verir. Yeni sanayilerin hızla yerini alması işsizliği düşürürdü, 'so that' anlamsız bir amaç kurar, 'even though' gereksiz bir zıtlık yaratır, 'unless ... will' ise dil bilgisi açısından hatalıdır.

questions.text: No sooner had the railway reached the small town ----.
options: when merchants began to open new shops
that it soon became a busy trading centre
than its population began to grow rapidly
than its population had been shrinking for years
before the first station was completed
questions.explanation: 'No sooner had ... than' (... -er -mez) kalıbı 'than' ile tamamlanır ve ardından geçmiş zaman gelir: Demiryolu kasabaya ulaşır ulaşmaz nüfus hızla artmaya başladı. 'When', 'that' ve 'before' bu kalıpla kullanılmaz; 'than ... had been shrinking' ise zaman ve anlam açısından kalıba uymaz.

questions.text: While earlier historians focused mainly on kings, wars and treaties, ----.
options: they relied heavily on official documents and chronicles
most of these treaties were signed in the eighteenth century by the major European powers
because ordinary people rarely left written records
social historians have turned their attention to the daily lives of ordinary people
kings were usually portrayed as heroic figures
questions.explanation: Burada 'while' (-iken, oysa) iki yaklaşımı karşılaştırır: eski tarihçiler krallara ve savaşlara odaklanırken sosyal tarihçiler sıradan insanların günlük yaşamına yönelmiştir. Resmî belgelere dayanmak ve antlaşmaların tarihi zıtlık kurmaz, krallar hakkındaki bilgi karşılaştırmayı tamamlamaz; 'because' ile başlayan seçenek ise yapıya dil bilgisi açısından uymaz.

questions.text:
Aşağıdaki İngilizce cümlenin anlamca en yakın Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir?

Archaeologists believe that the settlement was abandoned not because of a war but because of a prolonged drought that destroyed its crops.
options: Arkeologlara göre yerleşim yeri, ekinleri yok eden bir savaşın ardından uzun süren bir kuraklık nedeniyle terk edilmiştir.
Arkeologlar, yerleşim yerinin hem bir savaş hem de ekinleri yok eden uzun süreli bir kuraklık yüzünden terk edildiğini düşünmektedir.
Arkeologlar, ekinleri yok eden uzun süreli kuraklığın yerleşim yerinde bir savaşa yol açtığına inanmaktadır.
Arkeologlar, yerleşim yerinin bir savaş nedeniyle değil, ekinlerini yok eden uzun süreli bir kuraklık nedeniyle terk edildiğine inanmaktadır.
Arkeologlar, yerleşim yerinin uzun süreli bir kuraklık nedeniyle değil, ekinlerini yok eden uzun bir savaş nedeniyle terk edildiğine inanmaktadır.
questions.explanation: 'Not because of a war but because of a prolonged drought' yapısı 'bir savaş nedeniyle değil, uzun süreli bir kuraklık nedeniyle' biçiminde çevrilir; 'prolonged' (uzun süreli) ve 'abandoned' (terk edilmiş) doğru karşılanmıştır. Diğer seçenekler savaşı da neden olarak sayar, kuraklığı savaşın nedeni yapar ya da savaş ile kuraklığın yerini değiştirir.

questions.text:
Aşağıdaki İngilizce cümlenin anlamca en yakın Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir?

The rapid growth of cities in the nineteenth century created serious public health problems, which eventually led to the construction of modern sewage systems.
options: On dokuzuncu yüzyılda modern kanalizasyon sistemlerinin inşası, kentlerin hızla büyümesine ve ciddi halk sağlığı sorunlarına neden olmuştur.
On dokuzuncu yüzyılda hızla büyüyen kentlerde ciddi halk sağlığı sorunları yaşanmasına rağmen modern kanalizasyon sistemleri ancak çok sonraki dönemlerde inşa edilmiştir.
Kentlerin on dokuzuncu yüzyıldaki hızlı büyümesi, modern kanalizasyon sistemleri inşa edilmediği için ciddi halk sağlığı sorunları yaratmıştır.
On dokuzuncu yüzyılda kentler hızla büyüseydi, ciddi halk sağlığı sorunları ortaya çıkar ve modern kanalizasyon sistemleri inşa edilirdi.
On dokuzuncu yüzyılda kentlerin hızla büyümesi ciddi halk sağlığı sorunları yaratmış, bu da sonunda modern kanalizasyon sistemlerinin inşa edilmesine yol açmıştır.
questions.explanation: Cümlede neden-sonuç zinciri vardır: hızlı kentleşme halk sağlığı sorunları yaratmış, 'which eventually led to' (bu da sonunda ... yol açmıştır) ifadesiyle de bu sorunlar kanalizasyon sistemlerinin yapılmasını sağlamıştır. Diğer seçenekler bu sırayı tersine çevirir, 'rağmen' ile zıtlık kurar, kanalizasyon eksikliğini neden gösterir ya da cümleyi koşul cümlesine dönüştürür.

questions.text:
Aşağıdaki İngilizce cümlenin anlamca en yakın Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir?

Few economists had predicted that the crisis would spread so quickly from the banking sector to the rest of the economy.
options: Krizin bankacılık sektöründen ekonominin geri kalanına bu kadar hızlı yayılacağını çok az ekonomist öngörmüştü.
Birkaç ekonomist, krizin bankacılık sektöründen ekonominin geri kalanına hızla yayılacağını öngörmüştü.
Ekonomistlerin çoğu, krizin ekonominin geri kalanından bankacılık sektörüne bu kadar hızlı yayılacağını tahmin etmişti.
Çok az ekonomist, krizin bankacılık sektöründe başlayıp ekonominin geri kalanına yayılmayacağını öngörmüştü.
Krizin bankacılık sektöründen ekonominin geri kalanına yayılması, birçok ekonomistin öngördüğünden daha yavaş olmuştu.
questions.explanation: 'Few' (çok az) olumsuz bir anlam taşır ve 'so quickly' (bu kadar hızlı) vurgusuyla birlikte doğru biçimde 'çok az ekonomist öngörmüştü' olarak çevrilmiştir. 'Birkaç' ifadesi 'a few' karşılığıdır ve olumsuz vurguyu kaybeder; diğer seçenekler yayılmanın yönünü, olumlu/olumsuz anlamı ya da hızını değiştirir.

Gotik katedrallerin yüksek pencereleri, yalnızca iç mekânı aydınlatmak için değil, aynı zamanda ziyaretçilere dini hikâyeler anlatmak için de tasarlanmıştı.
options: The tall windows of Gothic cathedrals were designed to light the interior rather than to tell religious stories to visitors.
Visitors to Gothic cathedrals were told religious stories so that they could appreciate the tall windows lighting the interior.
The tall windows of Gothic cathedrals had been designed not only to light the interior but also to tell religious stories to visitors.
Although the tall windows of Gothic cathedrals lit the interior, they were not designed to tell religious stories to visitors.
The tall windows of Gothic cathedrals, which told religious stories to visitors, were later redesigned in order to light the interior better.
questions.explanation: 'Yalnızca ... değil, aynı zamanda ... de' yapısı 'not only ... but also' ile karşılanır ve pencerelerin iki amaçla tasarlandığını anlatır. 'Rather than' ve 'although ... not designed' seçenekleri ikinci amacı dışlar; diğerleri ise ziyaretçileri özne yaparak ya da 'later redesigned' (sonradan yeniden tasarlandı) diyerek anlamı değiştirir.

Kırsal bölgelerden kentlere göç arttıkça, geleneksel aile yapısı da önemli ölçüde değişmeye başladı.
options: Migration from cities to rural areas increased because the traditional family structure had changed considerably.
As migration from rural areas to cities increased, the traditional family structure also began to change considerably.
Unless migration from rural areas to cities increases, the traditional family structure will not change considerably in the future.
Although migration from rural areas to cities increased, the traditional family structure changed only slightly.
The traditional family structure began to change considerably before migration from rural areas to cities increased.
questions.explanation: '-dıkça' eki iki sürecin birlikte ilerlediğini anlatır ve 'as' (-dıkça) ile karşılanır; 'önemli ölçüde' 'considerably', 'değişmeye başladı' ise 'began to change' olarak doğru çevrilmiştir. Diğer seçenekler göçün yönünü ya da neden-sonuç ilişkisini tersine çevirir, cümleyi koşul cümlesine dönüştürür, zıtlık kurar veya olayların sırasını değiştirir.

questions.passage: For much of the discipline's history, archaeologists were drawn to monumental remains: temples, palaces and the tombs of rulers. Such sites, however, tell us mainly about elites, who made up only a small fraction of any ancient population. In recent decades, a growing number of researchers have turned their attention to a far humbler source of evidence: rubbish. Ancient refuse heaps, known as middens, accumulated gradually as households discarded broken pottery, animal bones, shells and ash. Because these deposits built up layer by layer, often over centuries, they preserve a remarkably continuous record of everyday life. By analysing the bones in a midden, for instance, specialists can determine which animals were eaten, at what age they were slaughtered and even whether meat was shared out evenly or reserved for certain households. Charred seeds reveal which crops were cultivated and how diets shifted when new plants were introduced. Middens are not without their problems, though. Unlike a sealed tomb, a rubbish heap was constantly disturbed by scavenging dogs, digging children and later builders, so objects from different periods can become mixed. Moreover, what people threw away is not necessarily what they used most; valuable items were often repaired or recycled rather than discarded, and so they are underrepresented. Careful excavators therefore combine midden data with other evidence, such as house plans and written sources where these exist. Despite these limitations, the study of refuse has transformed our picture of the past, shifting attention from the deeds of kings to the routines of ordinary farmers, fishers and craftspeople.
questions.text: The passage is mainly concerned with ----.
options: ways in which monumental sites were misinterpreted by early archaeologists
the value and limitations of ancient refuse heaps as evidence of ordinary people's lives
the reasons why ancient households recycled their most valuable objects
a comparison between tombs and palaces as sources of archaeological evidence
the techniques that specialists use to date the animal bones and charred seeds found at excavations
questions.explanation: Parça, 'midden' denilen antik çöp yığınlarının sıradan insanların gündelik yaşamı hakkında sunduğu bilgileri ve bu kaynağın sınırlılıklarını (karışan katmanlar, değerli eşyaların az bulunması) birlikte ele alır. Değerli eşyaların geri dönüştürülmesi yalnızca bir ayrıntıdır; tarihleme teknikleri ya da mezar-saray karşılaştırması parçanın konusu değildir.

questions.passage: In the towns of medieval Europe, most skilled trades were organised into guilds, associations of craftsmen who practised the same occupation. A guild set the standards that goods had to meet, fixed the length of apprenticeships and, in many cases, limited the number of workshops that could operate in a town. For a long time, economic historians regarded these organisations as essentially harmful. By restricting entry and controlling prices, it was argued, guilds protected the incomes of their members at the expense of consumers and slowed the spread of new techniques. This view owed much to eighteenth-century reformers, who campaigned to abolish guild privileges in the name of free trade. More recent scholarship has painted a more nuanced picture. Some historians point out that in an age with weak courts and little formal regulation, guilds performed useful functions. By inspecting products, they reassured distant buyers about quality, which encouraged long-distance trade. Their apprenticeship systems, moreover, offered a structured way of transmitting complex skills from one generation to the next at a time when there were no technical schools. Critics of this revisionist view respond that such benefits could have been provided by other institutions, and that guilds frequently used their influence over town councils to block competitors, including women and migrants. The debate remains unresolved, partly because guilds varied enormously: a powerful merchants' guild in a large trading city behaved very differently from a small association of rural weavers. What seems clear is that sweeping generalisations, whether favourable or hostile, rarely do justice to the evidence.
questions.text: According to the passage, the traditional view of guilds ----.
options: was first challenged by eighteenth-century reformers
emphasised their role in promoting long-distance trade
was shaped to a considerable extent by those who wished to abolish them
has been fully confirmed by recent research
was based mainly on evidence from small rural weaving associations rather than merchant guilds
questions.explanation: Parçaya göre loncaları zararlı gören geleneksel görüş büyük ölçüde ('owed much to') serbest ticaret adına lonca ayrıcalıklarının kaldırılması ('abolish': kaldırmak) için mücadele eden 18. yüzyıl reformcularına dayanır. Reformcular bu görüşü sorgulamamış, aksine desteklemiştir; uzun mesafeli ticarete katkı ise yeni araştırmaların vurguladığı bir noktadır ve yeni çalışmalar görüşü doğrulamamış, daha nüanslı hâle getirmiştir.

questions.passage: Since 1950, the share of the world's population living in cities has risen from under a third to more than half, and most of this growth has occurred in the developing world. Because formal housing markets in these countries have rarely kept pace with the arrival of rural migrants, a large proportion of newcomers have built their own homes on land they do not legally own. Such informal settlements, which often begin as clusters of makeshift shelters on the edges of cities, were long treated by governments as a temporary problem to be cleared away. Bulldozing, however, seldom achieved its aim: residents who were evicted from one site simply rebuilt elsewhere, usually in even worse conditions. From the 1970s onwards, a number of planners began to argue that informal settlements should be seen not as a failure but as evidence of the initiative of the urban poor. Observing that many shacks were gradually replaced by solid brick houses as families saved money, they proposed that governments should support this process by granting legal titles and providing basic services such as water, sewers and roads. This approach, often called 'upgrading', has since been adopted in many countries, with mixed results. Where secure ownership was granted, households frequently invested in improving their homes. Elsewhere, however, upgraded neighbourhoods became attractive to wealthier buyers, and the original residents were gradually priced out, a pattern that critics describe as displacement by the market rather than by the bulldozer.
questions.text: According to the passage, attempts to demolish informal settlements ----.
options: were largely successful in reducing the size of cities
were first proposed by planners in the 1970s
encouraged residents to obtain legal titles to the land on which they had built
generally failed because displaced people resettled elsewhere
led to a sharp rise in the price of formal housing
questions.explanation: Parçada yıkım politikasının ('bulldozing') amacına nadiren ulaştığı, çünkü tahliye edilen ('evicted') sakinlerin başka bir yerde, genellikle daha kötü koşullarda yeniden ev kurduğu belirtilir. 1970'lerde planlamacılar yıkımı değil, iyileştirmeyi ('upgrading') önermiştir; tapu verilmesi de yıkımın değil, bu yeni yaklaşımın parçasıdır.

questions.passage: Few questions in architectural conservation have generated as much controversy as the extent to which a damaged historic building ought to be restored. In the nineteenth century, many restorers believed that their task was to return a monument to the condition its original builders had intended, even if that condition had never actually existed. Guided by this principle, they removed later additions, replaced worn carvings with new ones and sometimes completed towers that had been left unfinished for centuries. Opponents of this practice, most famously the English critic John Ruskin, condemned it as a kind of forgery. In their view, the marks left on a building by time and by successive generations of users were themselves part of its value, and to erase them was to destroy the very authenticity that made the building worth preserving. Modern conservation charters largely reflect this second position. They generally require that any new material be distinguishable from the old on close inspection, and that interventions be kept to the minimum necessary to ensure a structure's survival. Yet the principle is easier to state than to apply. When a cathedral roof collapses in a fire, for instance, leaving the interior open to the sky would hardly preserve the building, while reconstructing the roof in modern materials might alter its character. Each case, therefore, demands judgement rather than the mechanical application of rules, and conservators frequently find themselves balancing the claims of history, safety and public expectation.

questions.passage: The idea that working people are entitled to regular periods of free time seems so natural today that it is easy to forget how recent it is. In pre-industrial Europe, labour was organised largely around the seasons and the tasks at hand; periods of intense work during the harvest alternated with slacker months and with numerous religious holidays. The rise of the factory changed this pattern fundamentally. Machines were expensive, and owners wanted them running continuously, so workers were subjected to long, fixed hours enforced by bells and clocks. In the early nineteenth century, shifts of twelve hours or more, six days a week, were common in the textile mills of Britain. It was against this background that the modern weekend gradually took shape. Some workers had long observed an unofficial holiday known as 'Saint Monday', simply failing to appear on the first day of the week, much to the frustration of employers. Over time, a compromise emerged in which a half-day on Saturday was granted in exchange for regular attendance on Monday. Trade unions, meanwhile, campaigned for shorter hours, and religious groups supported the change in the hope that workers with a free Saturday afternoon would be more likely to attend church on Sunday. Sociologists have noted that the new free time did not remain empty for long: it was quickly filled by organised activities such as football matches, seaside excursions and music halls, which in turn created entire industries devoted to leisure. In this sense, the weekend was not merely a break from the economy but a new arena of it.

Hasat dönemi sanayi öncesi düzene aittir; sendikalar ise kısa çalışma saatleri için mücadele etmiştir, bunu reddetmemiştir.

questions.text: Unless stricter emission limits are introduced soon, ----.

'Had already switched' ve 'was signed' geçmiş zamandadır; 'would have become' geçmişe dair gerçek dışı bir durumdur; bilim insanlarının karbon düzeyini izlemesi ise koşula bağlı bir sonuç değildir.

questions.passage: Permafrost, ground that remains frozen for at least two consecutive years, covers roughly a quarter of the exposed land in the Northern Hemisphere. Locked within it is an enormous store of organic matter: the remains of plants and animals that accumulated over thousands of years but never fully decomposed because the cold slowed microbial activity almost to a halt. Scientists estimate that this frozen soil holds nearly twice as much carbon as is currently present in the atmosphere. As the Arctic warms at a rate considerably faster than the global average, this carbon is becoming vulnerable. When permafrost thaws, microbes resume their work, breaking down the organic material and releasing carbon dioxide and, in waterlogged conditions, methane, a gas that traps far more heat over the short term. The worry is that such emissions could create a feedback loop, in which warming causes thaw and thaw causes further warming. Yet the picture is not straightforward. Thawing ground can also encourage the growth of shrubs and other vegetation, which absorb carbon and may partly offset the losses. Moreover, thaw does not always proceed gradually; in some regions, ice-rich ground collapses suddenly, forming lakes and slumps that expose deep layers within a few years rather than centuries. Such abrupt processes are poorly represented in most climate models, which means that current projections may underestimate the problem. For this reason, many researchers argue that expanding monitoring networks across the remote Arctic is no longer optional but an urgent scientific priority.
questions.text: According to the passage, the organic matter in permafrost has not fully decomposed because ----.
options: it has been buried too deep for any microbes to reach it
low temperatures have kept microbial activity extremely slow
it consists mainly of materials that cannot be broken down
the Arctic has warmed more slowly than the rest of the planet
waterlogged soils have prevented oxygen from reaching it
questions.explanation: Parçada organik maddenin binlerce yıl boyunca tam olarak ayrışmadığı, çünkü soğuğun mikrobik faaliyeti neredeyse durma noktasına kadar yavaşlattığı belirtiliyor; 'decompose' (ayrışmak, çürümek). Maddenin çok derinde olması ya da ayrışamayan malzemeden oluşması parçada geçmez. Kuzey Kutbu'nun daha yavaş ısındığı bilgisi ise parçanın tam tersidir.

questions.passage: Permafrost, ground that remains frozen for at least two consecutive years, covers roughly a quarter of the exposed land in the Northern Hemisphere. Locked within it is an enormous store of organic matter: the remains of plants and animals that accumulated over thousands of years but never fully decomposed because the cold slowed microbial activity almost to a halt. Scientists estimate that this frozen soil holds nearly twice as much carbon as is currently present in the atmosphere. As the Arctic warms at a rate considerably faster than the global average, this carbon is becoming vulnerable. When permafrost thaws, microbes resume their work, breaking down the organic material and releasing carbon dioxide and, in waterlogged conditions, methane, a gas that traps far more heat over the short term. The worry is that such emissions could create a feedback loop, in which warming causes thaw and thaw causes further warming. Yet the picture is not straightforward. Thawing ground can also encourage the growth of shrubs and other vegetation, which absorb carbon and may partly offset the losses. Moreover, thaw does not always proceed gradually; in some regions, ice-rich ground collapses suddenly, forming lakes and slumps that expose deep layers within a few years rather than centuries. Such abrupt processes are poorly represented in most climate models, which means that current projections may underestimate the problem. For this reason, many researchers argue that expanding monitoring networks across the remote Arctic is no longer optional but an urgent scientific priority.
questions.text: It can be inferred from the passage that current climate projections ----.
options: may not fully capture how quickly some permafrost can thaw
exaggerate the amount of carbon stored in frozen Arctic soils
already include detailed data from Arctic monitoring networks
show that new vegetation will completely cancel out emissions
predict that methane emissions will soon stop altogether
questions.explanation: Parçada ani çökme süreçlerinin iklim modellerinde yetersiz temsil edildiği ve bu yüzden tahminlerin sorunu olduğundan küçük gösterebileceği ('underestimate' – hafife almak) söyleniyor. Buradan modellerin bazı donmuş toprakların ne kadar hızlı çözülebildiğini tam yansıtmadığı sonucu çıkar. Bitki örtüsünün emisyonları tamamen sıfırlayacağı iddiası parçadaki 'partly' (kısmen) ifadesiyle çelişir; karbon miktarının abartıldığı da söylenmez.

questions.passage: Solar and wind power have become the cheapest sources of new electricity in many parts of the world, but their output depends on the weather and the time of day. This variability, known as intermittency, poses a serious challenge for grid operators, who must match supply and demand second by second. For decades, the gap was filled mainly by gas-fired power plants, which can be switched on and off relatively quickly. Today, large battery installations are increasingly taking over this role. Lithium-ion batteries, whose costs have fallen by roughly 90 percent over the past fifteen years, can absorb surplus electricity at midday and release it during the evening peak. However, they are best suited to storing energy for a few hours, not for days or entire seasons. A windless week in winter, for instance, cannot be covered by today's batteries alone. Engineers are therefore exploring a range of alternatives for long-duration storage. Some designs pump water uphill into reservoirs and let it flow down through turbines when power is needed; others compress air in underground caverns or store heat in molten salt or crushed rock. Hydrogen produced by electrolysis is another candidate, although converting electricity into hydrogen and back again wastes a large share of the original energy. No single technology is likely to dominate. Instead, experts expect future grids to combine several forms of storage with stronger transmission links, which allow regions with surplus power to supply those experiencing a shortfall, and with measures that encourage consumers to shift their use to times of abundance.
questions.text: According to the passage, the term 'intermittency' refers to ----.
options: the rapid fall in the cost of solar and wind installations
the time needed to switch gas-fired power plants on and off
the dependence of solar and wind output on weather and time of day
the loss of energy that occurs when electricity is turned into hydrogen
the difficulty of building transmission links between distant regions
questions.explanation: Parçanın ilk iki cümlesinde güneş ve rüzgâr üretiminin hava durumuna ve günün saatine bağlı olduğu, bu değişkenliğe 'intermittency' (kesintililik, süreksizlik) dendiği açıkça belirtiliyor. Maliyet düşüşü, gaz santrallerinin hızı ve hidrojen dönüşümündeki enerji kaybı parçada geçse de bu terimle ilgili değildir.

questions.passage: Since the launch of Sputnik in 1957, humanity has placed thousands of objects into orbit around the Earth, and not all of them have been removed once their missions ended. Defunct satellites, spent rocket stages and fragments from collisions and explosions now circle the planet at speeds of several kilometres per second. At such velocities, even a fragment the size of a coin can strike with the energy of a small explosive, and space agencies already track tens of thousands of pieces large enough to be catalogued. The concern most frequently raised by researchers is a scenario first described in the late 1970s, in which the density of objects in certain orbits becomes so high that one collision generates debris that triggers further collisions, in a chain reaction that could render some orbital zones unusable for generations. The recent rise of so-called mega-constellations, in which a single company may operate thousands of small satellites, has made this risk harder to ignore. Proponents argue that these satellites fly in low orbits, where atmospheric drag pulls failed spacecraft back to Earth within a few years. Critics respond that the sheer number of launches reduces the margin for error and complicates the work of astronomers, whose images are increasingly crossed by bright streaks. Several technical solutions have been proposed, from nets and harpoons that would capture old satellites to lasers that would nudge small fragments into lower orbits. Nevertheless, most experts agree that technology alone will not solve the problem without international rules that oblige operators to dispose of their spacecraft responsibly.
questions.text: According to the passage, even very small pieces of space debris are dangerous because ----.
options: they are too small to be detected by any space agency
they contain explosive material left over from rocket stages
they reflect sunlight and blind the instruments of satellites
they gradually fall back to Earth and damage populated areas
they move fast enough to strike with considerable force
questions.explanation: Parçada saniyede birkaç kilometrelik hızlarda madeni para büyüklüğündeki bir parçanın bile küçük bir patlayıcı enerjisiyle çarpabileceği söyleniyor; 'velocity' (hız). Yani tehlike, parçaların yüksek hızından kaynaklanır. Parçaların patlayıcı içerdiği, aletleri kör ettiği ya da yerleşim yerlerine düştüğü söylenmez; kurumların on binlerce parçayı izlediği de belirtilir.

questions.passage: Of the roughly 7,000 languages spoken in the world today, only a small fraction are well represented on the internet. This imbalance has become particularly significant with the rise of artificial intelligence systems that learn from vast collections of digital text. Machine translation tools and voice assistants perform impressively in English, Chinese or Spanish, for which billions of words are available, but they often struggle with languages that have few written resources, even when those languages have millions of speakers. Linguists refer to such languages as 'low-resource', a label that describes the scarcity of data rather than any deficiency in the languages themselves. The consequences extend beyond inconvenience. As more public services, educational materials and job opportunities move online, speakers of under-represented languages may find themselves at a disadvantage, and younger generations may come to see their mother tongue as unsuited to modern life. Some researchers have responded by developing methods that allow a model trained on resource-rich languages to transfer part of its knowledge to related languages with limited data. Others emphasise community-led projects in which native speakers record stories, transcribe conversations and correct machine output. Such initiatives, however, raise difficult questions about ownership: communities that have historically had their cultural heritage taken without consent are understandably wary of handing their words to large technology firms. Several projects have therefore adopted licensing agreements that keep control of the data in the hands of the speakers. Whether these efforts can keep pace with the rapid expansion of AI remains uncertain, but they demonstrate that technological progress need not come at the expense of linguistic diversity.
questions.text: According to the passage, the term 'low-resource' ----.
options: applies only to languages with fewer than a million speakers living in a single country
means that a language has a simple and limited grammar
is used for languages that have no written form at all
refers to a lack of available data rather than a weakness of the language
describes languages that are no longer taught in schools
questions.explanation: Parçada 'low-resource' etiketinin dillerin kendisindeki bir eksikliği ('deficiency' – yetersizlik) değil, verinin azlığını ('scarcity' – kıtlık) anlattığı açıkça belirtiliyor. Bu dillerin milyonlarca konuşanı olabileceği söylendiği için konuşan sayısına dayalı tanım yanlıştır; dil bilgisinin basitliği ya da yazısız olma gibi bilgiler parçada yer almaz.

Belirsizlik vurgusu 'unreservedly enthusiastic' (çekincesiz coşkulu) tutumu, olumlu sonuç cümlesi de 'deeply pessimistic' (son derece karamsar) tutumu dışlar.

questions.passage: Ask most students how they prepare for an exam, and many will describe rereading their notes or highlighting key passages in their textbooks. These strategies feel productive because the material becomes increasingly familiar with each pass. Research in cognitive psychology, however, suggests that familiarity is a poor guide to learning. A large body of studies has shown that students remember far more when they actively try to recall information, for instance by answering practice questions or writing down everything they can remember about a topic without looking at their notes. This phenomenon, known as the testing effect or retrieval practice, appears to work because the effort of retrieving a memory strengthens the pathways that lead to it, making it easier to access in the future. Interestingly, the benefits are greatest when retrieval is somewhat difficult; questions that can be answered effortlessly do little to consolidate knowledge. The effect is further enhanced when practice sessions are spaced out over days or weeks instead of being crammed into a single evening. Despite this evidence, retrieval practice remains underused in many classrooms. One reason is that teachers and students often associate tests with grades and anxiety rather than with learning. Another is that the strategy feels less comfortable than rereading: struggling to recall something creates an impression of failure, even when it is precisely this struggle that produces durable memories. Educational researchers therefore recommend that low-stakes quizzes, which do not count towards final marks, be integrated into everyday teaching.
questions.text: According to the passage, many students prefer rereading their notes because ----.
options: their teachers usually require them to do so before exams
growing familiarity with the material gives them a sense of progress
it has been proven to produce more durable memories than testing or answering practice questions
it allows them to study for many weeks instead of one evening
practice questions are rarely available in their textbooks
questions.explanation: Parçaya göre tekrar okuma ve önemli yerleri işaretleme, malzeme her okumada daha tanıdık ('familiar') hâle geldiği için verimli hissettirir; yani öğrenciler ilerleme kaydettiklerini düşünür. Tekrar okumanın daha kalıcı bellek sağladığı iddiası parçanın tam tersidir; öğretmenlerin bunu zorunlu kılması ya da alıştırma sorularının bulunmaması ise parçada geçmez.

questions.text: It is stated in the passage that retrieval practice is most effective when ----.
options: the questions can be answered without any effort
all practice sessions take place on a single evening
students look at their notes while answering the practice questions they have been given
recalling the information requires a certain amount of effort

Tek akşamda yoğun çalışma, notlara bakarak cevaplama ve notu etkileyen sınavlar parçada önerilenin tersidir.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT given in the passage as a reason why retrieval practice is underused?
options: Tests are often linked with grades in people's minds.
Tests can make students feel anxious.
It takes up too much time in a crowded curriculum.
Struggling to recall information may feel like failing.
It feels less comfortable than rereading notes.
questions.explanation: Parçada geri çağırma pratiğinin az kullanılmasının nedenleri olarak sınavların notlarla ve kaygıyla ('anxiety') ilişkilendirilmesi ile yöntemin tekrar okumadan daha az rahat hissettirmesi ve zorlanmanın başarısızlık izlenimi yaratması sayılıyor. Yoğun bir müfredatta fazla zaman alması ise hiç belirtilmiyor; bu yüzden doğru cevap budur.

questions.text: The passage is mainly concerned with ----.
options: the history of examinations in modern school systems
the negative effects of exam anxiety on students' health
the reasons why highlighting is the best way to study
the brain regions responsible for long-term memory
a learning strategy that is effective but not widely applied
questions.explanation: Parça, geri çağırma pratiğinin ('retrieval practice') öğrenmede çok etkili olduğunu gösteren araştırmaları ve buna rağmen sınıflarda yeterince kullanılmamasının nedenlerini anlatıyor; ana fikir budur. Sınav kaygısı yalnızca bir neden olarak geçer; işaretlemenin en iyi yöntem olduğu fikri ise parçanın savunduğunun tersidir.

questions.passage:
Emma: Did you see that the council is planning to plant ten thousand trees along the main roads?
Daniel: Yes, but I'm not sure it will make much of a difference to air quality.
Emma: ----
Daniel: Fair enough. I hadn't thought about the cooling effect in summer.
Emma: Exactly. Shaded streets can be several degrees cooler, which matters more and more as heatwaves become common.
questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Perhaps not directly, but trees also lower street temperatures, which is just as important.
I agree; the council should spend the money on something else entirely.
They plan to finish the planting by the end of next year.
Most of the trees will be native species chosen by local experts.
Air quality in the city centre has improved a lot since the new traffic rules were introduced last year.
questions.explanation: Daniel'in cevabındaki 'I hadn't thought about the cooling effect' (serinletici etkiyi düşünmemiştim) ifadesi, Emma'nın ağaçların sokak sıcaklığını düşürdüğünden söz ettiğini gösterir. Paranın başka işe harcanması gerektiği, dikimin ne zaman biteceği ya da yerli türler seçileceği gibi cevaplar serinletme etkisine bağlanmaz.

questions.passage:
Leyla: We're thinking of replacing our old gas boiler with a heat pump.
Mark: Good idea. But have you checked how well your house is insulated?
Leyla: Not really. Why does that matter?
Mark: ----
Leyla: I see. So we should probably deal with the insulation first.
questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Gas prices have risen sharply in most European countries this year.
My neighbour installed one last winter and is very pleased with it.
Heat pumps work at lower temperatures, so a poorly insulated house may never feel warm enough.
You can usually get a government grant that covers a large part of the cost of buying and installing one.
Heat pumps are much quieter than they used to be ten years ago.
questions.explanation: Leyla yalıtımın neden önemli olduğunu soruyor ve ardından önce yalıtımla ilgilenmeleri gerektiği sonucuna varıyor. Bu nedenle Mark'ın, ısı pompalarının düşük sıcaklıkta çalıştığını ve yalıtımı ('insulation') zayıf bir evin yeterince ısınmayabileceğini açıklaması gerekir. Gaz fiyatları, devlet desteği ya da cihazların sessizliği yalıtım sorusunu yanıtlamaz.

questions.passage:
Professor Hale: I've noticed that several essays this term contain almost identical phrasing.
Dr Kaya: Do you think the students used an AI writing tool?
Professor Hale: ----
Dr Kaya: That's a sensible approach. Asking them to explain their arguments face to face should reveal a lot.
Professor Hale: Yes, and it treats them fairly rather than assuming they cheated.
questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Certainly, so I've already failed all of them without any further discussion or chance to explain.
Possibly, but before accusing anyone, I'd like to talk to each of them about their work.
No, I think the topic was simply too difficult for most of them.
I've never used such tools myself, so I can't really say.
They submitted the essays two days after the deadline.
questions.explanation: Dr Kaya'nın 'sensible approach' (makul yaklaşım) diyerek öğrencilerle yüz yüze konuşmaktan söz etmesi, Profesör Hale'in kimseyi suçlamadan ('accuse' – suçlamak) önce öğrencilerle görüşmek istediğini söylediğini gösterir. Hepsini doğrudan başarısız saymak 'treats them fairly' ifadesiyle çelişir; diğer seçenekler ise bir yaklaşım önermez.

questions.passage:
Nadia: Did you watch the launch of the new space telescope yesterday?
Tom: I did. What exactly is it going to study?
Nadia: ----
Tom: So it might eventually tell us whether any of those planets could support life?
Nadia: That's the hope, although it will take years of observations to be sure.
questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: It was built by a team of engineers from more than fifteen countries.
The launch had been delayed twice because of bad weather.
It cost far more than the original budget had allowed.
Mainly the atmospheres of planets orbiting other stars, looking for gases like water vapour.
It will orbit the Sun about one and a half million kilometres from Earth, well beyond the orbit of the Moon.
questions.explanation: Tom teleskobun neyi inceleyeceğini soruyor ve ardından 'those planets' (o gezegenler) diyerek yaşam ihtimalinden söz ediyor; demek ki Nadia başka yıldızların çevresindeki gezegenlerin atmosferlerinden bahsetmiştir. Mühendisler, gecikme, maliyet ya da yörünge bilgisi teleskobun ne inceleyeceğini açıklamaz ve gezegenlerden söz etmez.

questions.passage:
Ali: I'm thinking about taking an online course instead of attending classes on campus next year.
Ms Carter: That could work, but online learning requires a lot of self-discipline.
Ali: ----
Ms Carter: In that case, you'd probably benefit from the structure of face-to-face classes, at least for now.
Ali: You may be right. I'll think it over before I decide.
questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: I've always been very good at organising my own time.
The online courses are also considerably cheaper.
Many of my friends have already enrolled in online programmes.
The campus is quite far from where I live.
To be honest, I often put off assignments until the last minute.
questions.explanation: Ms Carter 'In that case' (o hâlde) diyerek yüz yüze derslerin düzeninden faydalanacağını söylüyor; bu, Ali'nin öz disiplin konusunda zayıf olduğunu, ödevlerini son dakikaya ertelediğini ('put off' – ertelemek) itiraf ettiğini gösterir. Zamanını iyi yönettiğini söylemesi bu öneriyle çelişir; ücret, arkadaşlar ya da mesafe ise disiplin konusuyla ilgili değildir.

questions.passage:
Sara: I read that somewhere in the world a language disappears roughly every few weeks.
James: That's alarming. But why should it matter to people who don't speak those languages?
Sara: ----
James: I hadn't considered that. So losing a language is a bit like losing a library.
Sara: Exactly, and often there's no copy of it anywhere else.
questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Because each language holds unique knowledge, for example about local plants and ecosystems.
Because learning a second language has been shown to improve memory and concentration in old age.
Most of them are spoken only in remote mountain villages.
Linguists have recorded only a few of them so far.
Because English is now the dominant language of science.
questions.explanation: James dil kaybını bir kütüphane kaybına benzetiyor; bu benzetme, Sara'nın her dilin yerel bitkiler ve ekosistemler gibi konularda eşsiz bilgi barındırdığını söylemesiyle anlam kazanır. İkinci dil öğrenmenin belleğe etkisi ya da İngilizcenin bilimdeki yeri soruyu yanıtlamaz; dillerin nerede konuşulduğu da 'neden önemli' sorusuna cevap değildir.

questions.text:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

Unless governments invest heavily in renewable energy over the next decade, it will be almost impossible to keep global warming below the agreed limit.
options: Governments have already invested heavily in renewable energy, so global warming will stay below the agreed limit.
Even if governments invest heavily in renewable energy, global warming will exceed the agreed limit within a decade.
Keeping global warming below the agreed limit will be nearly impossible if governments do not invest heavily in renewable energy in the coming ten years.
Over the next decade, governments will find it almost impossible to invest in renewable energy.
The agreed limit on global warming should be raised because renewable energy requires heavy investment.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' (-medikçe, eğer ... -mezse) yapısı 'if ... not' ile aynı anlamı verir: Hükümetler önümüzdeki on yılda yenilenebilir enerjiye büyük yatırım yapmazsa ısınmayı sınırın altında tutmak neredeyse imkânsız olacaktır. 'Even if' (-se bile) koşulun sonucu değiştirmediğini anlatır; yatırımın zaten yapıldığını ya da sınırın yükseltilmesi gerektiğini söyleyen cümleler asıl anlamı bozar.

questions.text:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

No sooner had the probe entered the planet's atmosphere than it began transmitting data that surprised the mission scientists.
options: The probe transmitted surprising data long before it reached the planet's atmosphere.
As soon as the probe entered the planet's atmosphere, it started sending data that surprised the mission scientists.
The mission scientists were surprised that the probe failed to send any data at all after entering the planet's atmosphere.
The probe entered the planet's atmosphere only after the scientists had analysed its surprising data.
The scientists had expected exactly the data that the probe sent after entering the atmosphere.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner had ... than ...' yapısı 'as soon as' (-er -mez) anlamı verir: Sonda atmosfere girer girmez bilim insanlarını şaşırtan veriler göndermeye başladı. Verilerin atmosfere girmeden çok önce gönderildiğini, hiç veri gelmediğini ya da verilerin beklendiğini söyleyen cümleler hem zaman ilişkisini hem de 'surprised' (şaşırmış) anlamını bozar.

questions.text:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

It is not so much the amount of time students spend studying as the way they study that determines how much they learn.
options: Students who spend more time studying always learn more, whatever methods they use.
The time spent studying and the way of studying are equally important for learning.
Students learn little mainly because they do not spend enough time studying.
How students study affects their learning more than how long they study.
The way students study depends largely on how much time they have.
questions.explanation: 'Not so much X as Y' (X'ten çok Y) yapısı Y'nin daha belirleyici olduğunu anlatır: Öğrenmeyi belirleyen, çalışma süresinden çok çalışma biçimidir. Sürenin her zaman daha önemli olduğunu ya da ikisinin eşit önemde olduğunu söyleyen cümleler bu karşılaştırmayı bozar; çalışma biçiminin süreye bağlı olduğu ise hiç söylenmemiştir.

questions.passage: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence has a cost that is often overlooked: electricity. Training a single large language model can consume as much energy as hundreds of households use in a year, and running such models for millions of users every day requires even more. ---- Some technology companies have responded by signing long-term contracts with wind and solar farms, while researchers are designing more efficient chips and algorithms that achieve similar results with less computation.
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Artificial intelligence was first proposed as a field of research in the 1950s.
Nevertheless, most users are still unaware of how large language models actually generate the text they read.
Solar panels, by contrast, have become far cheaper over the past decade.
In addition, AI systems are increasingly used to diagnose diseases in hospitals.
As a result, the data centres that run these systems are placing growing pressure on electricity grids.
questions.explanation: Paragraf yapay zekânın yüksek elektrik tüketimini anlatıyor ve boşluktan sonra şirketlerin bu soruna nasıl yanıt verdiği ('responded') açıklanıyor. Araya, bu tüketimin sonucu olarak veri merkezlerinin şebekeler üzerinde artan bir baskı oluşturduğunu söyleyen 'As a result' (sonuç olarak) cümlesi gelmelidir. Tarihçe, hastanelerde kullanım ya da güneş paneli fiyatları enerji sorunu akışını bozar.

questions.passage: ---- When carbon dioxide dissolves in seawater, it forms carbonic acid, which gradually lowers the water's pH. This change makes it harder for organisms such as corals, oysters and certain plankton to build their shells and skeletons from calcium carbonate. Because many of these species lie at the base of marine food webs, the effects could spread to fish populations and, ultimately, to the communities that depend on them.
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: The oceans absorb roughly a quarter of the carbon dioxide released by human activities, but this service comes at a price.
Coral reefs are among the most popular destinations for tourists in tropical regions.
Overfishing remains the greatest threat to marine biodiversity in most parts of the world.
Sea levels are rising mainly because warmer water expands and glaciers melt.
However, scientists have found that most shellfish adapt easily to more acidic water.
questions.explanation: Paragraf, okyanusa karışan karbondioksitin suyu asitleştirmesini ve deniz canlılarına etkisini anlatıyor; bu yüzden giriş cümlesi okyanusların insan kaynaklı karbondioksitin bir kısmını emdiğini ve bunun bir bedeli olduğunu söylemelidir. 'However' ile başlayan cümle hem giriş için uygun değildir hem de paragrafın anlattığı zararla çelişir; turizm, aşırı avlanma ve deniz seviyesi konu dışıdır.

questions.passage: Children across the world acquire their first language with remarkable speed and without formal instruction. By the age of four, most can produce complex sentences and follow conversations on a wide range of topics. ---- For example, a child who says 'I goed to the park' is not imitating adults, who never use this form, but applying the regular past-tense rule to an irregular verb. Such errors suggest that children actively construct grammatical rules rather than simply copying what they hear.
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Adults, in contrast, usually find it difficult to learn a new language.
Most parents read stories to their children before they go to sleep.
Interestingly, the mistakes they make along the way reveal a great deal about how this process works.
Some languages have far more irregular verbs than English does.
Therefore, children should begin learning a foreign language at school as early as possible.
questions.explanation: Boşluktan sonra 'For example' ile bir çocuğun yaptığı dil bilgisi hatası örnekleniyor ve 'Such errors' (bu tür hatalar) ifadesi geçiyor. Bu nedenle boşluğa, çocukların yaptığı hataların dil edinim sürecini ortaya koyduğunu söyleyen cümle gelmelidir. Yetişkinlerin dil öğrenmesi, düzensiz fiil sayısı ya da yabancı dil eğitimi önerisi örnekle bağlantı kurmaz.

questions.passage: For decades, the Moon was thought to be completely dry. However, data collected by orbiting spacecraft over the past twenty years have revealed water ice in permanently shadowed craters near the lunar poles, where temperatures never rise above about minus 160 degrees Celsius. This discovery has transformed plans for lunar exploration. Water could be melted for drinking and split into hydrogen and oxygen, which can be used both for breathing and as rocket fuel. ----
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: The Moon has no atmosphere to protect its surface from meteorites.
Using these local resources would greatly reduce the amount of material that must be launched from Earth at enormous cost.
The first humans landed on the Moon in 1969 during the Apollo 11 mission.
Nevertheless, craters near the lunar equator receive sunlight throughout the year.
As a result, scientists now believe that the Moon was formed from Earth's crust.
questions.explanation: Paragraf Ay'daki buzun içme suyu, solunacak oksijen ve roket yakıtı olarak kullanılabileceğini anlatıyor; mantıklı sonuç, bu yerel kaynakların ('local resources') Dünya'dan pahalıya fırlatılması gereken malzeme miktarını azaltacağıdır. Apollo 11, atmosfer yokluğu ya da Ay'ın oluşumu gibi bilgiler buzun Ay görevlerine sağlayacağı faydayı anlatan akışı tamamlamaz.

questions.passage: (I) Electronic waste, which includes discarded phones, computers and household appliances, is the fastest-growing category of solid waste in the world. (II) Much of it contains valuable metals such as gold, copper and cobalt, as well as hazardous substances like lead and mercury. (III) Yet only about a fifth of this waste is formally collected and recycled, while the rest is dumped, burned or handled by informal workers without protective equipment. (IV) Smartphones have also changed the way people communicate, allowing instant contact across continents. (V) Improving collection systems could therefore protect human health and, at the same time, recover materials worth billions of dollars every year.
questions.text: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
questions.explanation: Paragraf elektronik atıkların ('e-waste') değerli ve tehlikeli içeriğini, yetersiz geri dönüşümünü ve toplama sistemlerinin iyileştirilmesinin faydalarını anlatıyor. Akıllı telefonların iletişimi nasıl değiştirdiğinden söz eden dördüncü cümle atık konusuyla ilgisizdir ve akışı bozar; beşinci cümledeki 'therefore' (bu yüzden) doğrudan üçüncü cümleye bağlanır.

questions.passage: (I) When massive open online courses first appeared, many commentators predicted that they would make traditional universities obsolete. (II) Millions of learners signed up, attracted by free lectures from prestigious institutions. (III) However, completion rates turned out to be strikingly low, often below ten percent. (IV) Researchers found that the learners who succeeded tended to be those who already held degrees and had strong study habits. (V) The oldest universities in Europe, such as Bologna, were founded during the Middle Ages.
questions.text: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
questions.explanation: Paragraf, kitlesel açık çevrim içi derslerin geleneksel üniversitelerin yerini alacağı beklentisini, düşük tamamlama oranlarını ve başarılı öğrencilerin özelliklerini anlatıyor. Avrupa'nın en eski üniversitelerinin Orta Çağ'da kurulduğunu söyleyen beşinci cümle, 'university' kelimesini paylaşsa da çevrim içi eğitim konusundan kopuktur. 'Obsolete' (modası geçmiş, gereksiz) kelimesi ilk cümlenin anahtarıdır.

questions.passage: (I) Most of the planets discovered outside our solar system have been detected by the transit method. (II) The technique measures the tiny dip in a star's brightness that occurs when a planet passes in front of it. (III) Ancient astronomers named the planets of our own solar system after gods from Roman mythology. (IV) The size of the dip reveals the planet's diameter, while the time between dips shows how long the planet takes to complete an orbit. (V) However, the method only works when the planet's orbit is aligned with our line of sight, so many planets inevitably go unnoticed.
questions.text: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
questions.explanation: Paragraf, güneş sistemi dışındaki gezegenlerin geçiş yöntemiyle ('transit method') nasıl bulunduğunu, yöntemin neler ölçtüğünü ve sınırlılığını anlatıyor. Antik astronomların gezegenlere Roma tanrılarının adlarını verdiğini söyleyen üçüncü cümle bu yöntemle ilgisizdir; ayrıca dördüncü cümledeki 'the dip' (düşüş) ifadesi doğrudan ikinci cümleye bağlanır.

questions.passage: (I) For much of the twentieth century, many parents and teachers believed that raising a child with two languages would cause confusion and delay. (II) Many of the world's languages, in fact, have never developed a written form. (III) More recent research, however, has largely overturned this belief. (IV) Bilingual children may start speaking slightly later in each language, but their total vocabulary across both languages is usually comparable to that of their monolingual peers. (V) Some studies even suggest that regularly switching between languages strengthens the ability to focus attention and ignore distractions.

Dünya dillerinin çoğunun yazılı biçimi olmadığını söyleyen ikinci cümle iki dillilik konusuyla ilgisizdir; üçüncü cümledeki 'this belief' ifadesi de doğrudan birinci cümleye gönderme yapar.

questions.passage: (I) Mountaineering has become increasingly popular, and some famous peaks now attract long queues of climbers every season. (II) In many mountain regions, glaciers act as natural water towers, storing snow in winter and releasing meltwater during the dry summer months. (III) Hundreds of millions of people in Asia and South America depend on this seasonal flow for drinking water, farming and hydropower. (IV) As temperatures rise, many glaciers are shrinking rapidly, and in the short term this actually increases the amount of meltwater reaching rivers. (V) Once a glacier has shrunk beyond a certain point, however, the flow begins to decline, a turning point that scientists call 'peak water'.

options: I
II
III
IV
V

Dağcılığın popülerleşmesinden ve zirvelerdeki kuyruklardan söz eden birinci cümle, dağlarla ilgili olsa da buzulların su kaynağı rolüyle bağlantılı değildir ve anlam bütünlüğünü bozar.

questions.text: The volcanic eruption was so powerful that the ash it released ---- sunlight across much of the northern hemisphere for several months.

'Reinforced' (güçlendirmek) anlamı tersine çevirir; 'nourished' (beslemek), 'acquitted' (aklamak) ve 'summoned' (çağırmak) ise 'sunlight' ile anlamlı bir bağlam kurmaz.

questions.text: Nutritionists caution that many of the health claims printed on food packages are not ---- by rigorous scientific evidence.
options: substantiated
dispersed
contaminated
inhabited
abandoned
questions.explanation: 'Substantiated by evidence' (kanıtla desteklenmek, doğrulanmak) kalıbı, beslenme uzmanlarının ambalajdaki sağlık iddialarına yönelik uyarısıyla tam örtüşür. 'Contaminated' (kirlenmiş) ve 'dispersed' (dağıtılmış) kanıtla ilişkilendirilemez; 'inhabited' (yerleşilmiş) ve 'abandoned' (terk edilmiş) de iddiaların bilimsel dayanağını anlatmaz.

questions.text: As rents in the city centre continued to rise, many long-term residents were forced to ---- their homes and move to the outskirts.
options: look up to
set off
give up
turn down
make up for

'Turn down' (reddetmek) bir teklif için kullanılır, ev için anlamsızdır; 'look up to' (saygı duymak), 'set off' (yola çıkmak) ve 'make up for' (telafi etmek) de bağlama uymaz.

questions.text: Although the new alloy is ---- lighter than steel, it is almost as strong, which makes it ideal for aircraft parts.
options: reluctantly
mutually
faithfully
considerably
previously
questions.explanation: 'Although' ile kurulan zıtlık, alaşımın çelikten 'considerably' (önemli ölçüde) hafif olmasına rağmen neredeyse onun kadar güçlü olduğunu vurgular. 'Reluctantly' (isteksizce) ve 'faithfully' (sadakatle) cansız bir malzemeyi nitelemez; 'mutually' (karşılıklı olarak) ve 'previously' (önceden) de karşılaştırma sıfatı 'lighter' ile uyumlu değildir.

questions.text: Linguists generally reject the idea that some languages are inherently more ---- than others, arguing that every language fully meets the communicative needs of its speakers.

audible
contagious
reluctant
punctual

'Audible' (duyulabilir) ve 'punctual' (dakik) dilin değerini anlatmaz; 'contagious' (bulaşıcı) ve 'reluctant' (isteksiz) ise dil için anlamsızdır.

questions.text: The ministry's decision to cut funding for rural schools has provoked strong ---- from teachers' unions and parents alike.

questions.text: Geologists ---- the fault line for nearly forty years before the first major earthquake in the region was finally recorded in 2019.

are monitoring

monitor

'Have been monitoring' günümüze uzanan bir süreç bildirir ve 'was recorded' ile uyuşmaz; 'will have monitored' geleceğe, 'are monitoring' ve 'monitor' ise şimdiki zamana aittir.

questions.text: Judging by the old channels visible in satellite images, the river ---- its course several times over the past thousand years.

questions.text: Before the new curriculum ---- nationwide, it was tested in fifty pilot schools for two years.

was introduced

'Introduced' ve 'has introduced' etken yapıdadır ve nesneleri yoktur; 'had been introducing' ile 'is introducing' de hem etken hem de zaman bakımından uyumsuzdur.

questions.text: Neighbourhoods ---- residents frequently meet in shared public spaces tend to report higher levels of trust.

questions.text: People with high blood pressure are usually advised to avoid ---- large amounts of salt, as it can raise their blood pressure even further.

'All' ve 'Each' korozyon görüldüğünü söyler ki bu beklentiyle örtüşür, şaşkınlık yaratmaz; 'Both' ve 'Either' ise yalnızca iki öğe için kullanılır, burada üç örnek vardır.

questions.text: The study found that children's reading ability is closely linked ---- the number of books available in the home.

questions.text: Many residents now wish the city council ---- the historic market hall before it was demolished to make way for a car park.

protects

questions.text: Only after the soil samples had been analysed ---- that they contained dangerous levels of lead.

did the researchers realise
the researchers did realise

'The researchers realised' ve 'the researchers did realise' devrik değildir; 'had realised the researchers' ve 'realised the researchers' ise özne ile fiilin yerini yanlış biçimde değiştirir.

questions.passage: Sinkholes are depressions in the ground that form when water dissolves the rock beneath the surface. They are most common in regions (1) ---- the bedrock consists of limestone, gypsum or salt, all of which are slowly worn away by slightly acidic rainwater. In many cases, the process takes thousands of years, and the ground above (2) ---- gradually, producing a shallow bowl in the landscape. Occasionally, (3) ----, a cavity grows underground while the surface layer remains intact, until its roof suddenly collapses. Such events can swallow roads, cars and even buildings with little warning. Human activity often makes the problem worse: pumping large quantities of groundwater (4) ---- the support that water provides to the walls of underground cavities, and leaking pipes can wash away soil at an accelerated rate. (5) ----, engineers in vulnerable areas now use ground-penetrating radar to detect hidden voids before construction begins.

questions.passage: Dietary fibre, found in vegetables, whole grains and legumes, was long regarded simply as 'roughage' that helped food pass (1) ---- the digestive system. Researchers now know that it plays a far more complex role. Because human enzymes cannot break down most types of fibre, it reaches the large intestine largely intact, (2) ---- it becomes food for trillions of bacteria. As these microbes ferment the fibre, they produce short-chain fatty acids, compounds that (3) ---- to reduce inflammation and help regulate blood sugar. Despite these benefits, most adults in industrialised countries consume (4) ---- half the amount of fibre that health authorities recommend. Nutritionists suggest that increasing intake gradually is wise, since a sudden change in diet (5) ---- temporary bloating and discomfort.

questions.text: Unless schools receive adequate funding for teacher training, ----.

teachers have been complaining about their workload for years
it would have been introduced several years earlier

the new curriculum is unlikely to achieve its goals

'Had been welcomed' ve 'would have been introduced' zaman uyumunu bozar; öğretmen şikâyetleri ve çevrim içi öğrenme tercihi ise koşulun sonucu değildir.

So that residents could leave their homes quickly

questions.text: The longer a word has existed in a language, ----.
options: the more likely it is to have developed several different meanings
it will be used less and less frequently
so it becomes harder for learners to pronounce
the fewer speakers had known its origin
whereas new words appear in dictionaries every year in many different languages
questions.explanation: 'The longer …, the more …' karşılaştırmalı paralel yapı ikinci yarıda da 'the + karşılaştırma' gerektirir: 'the more likely it is to have developed several different meanings'. 'It will be used less …' ve 'so it becomes …' bu kalıbı tamamlamaz; 'the fewer speakers had known' zaman bakımından uyumsuzdur; 'whereas …' ise karşılaştırmayı tamamlamaz.

questions.text: Many urban planners now favour mixed-use neighbourhoods, ----.

questions.passage: Concrete is the most widely used construction material on Earth, yet it has a persistent weakness: it cracks. Even hairline fractures allow water and dissolved salts to seep inside, where they corrode the steel reinforcement and gradually weaken the entire structure. Repairing such damage is costly, and in places such as tunnels or deep foundations it is often impossible. In response, materials scientists have been experimenting with concrete that can mend itself. One promising approach involves mixing dormant bacterial spores, together with a source of calcium, into the wet concrete. The spores can survive for many years inside the hardened material. When a crack opens and water enters, they are reactivated and begin to produce limestone, which gradually fills the gap. In a recent trial at a coastal research station in Varden, test slabs containing the bacteria sealed cracks up to half a millimetre wide within six weeks, whereas ordinary slabs showed no recovery at all. Nevertheless, the technology faces obstacles. Self-healing concrete currently costs roughly twice as much as the conventional kind, and wider cracks remain beyond the bacteria's capacity. Some engineers also question whether the spores will remain viable after fifty or a hundred years, the lifespan expected of major infrastructure. Supporters respond that the higher initial price is likely to be recovered through reduced maintenance over a structure's lifetime.
questions.text: According to the passage, even very small cracks in concrete are a problem because ----.
options: they reduce the amount of calcium available to bacteria
they let in substances that damage the steel inside the structure
they cannot be detected without specialised equipment
they make concrete twice as expensive to produce
they are usually caused by bacteria growing inside the hardened material over time
questions.explanation: Parçada kılcal çatlakların bile su ve tuzların içeri sızmasına izin verdiği, bunların çelik donatıyı aşındırarak yapıyı zayıflattığı belirtilir; yani çatlaklar çeliğe zarar veren maddeleri içeri alır. Kalsiyum miktarı ya da özel ekipman gereksinimi parçada çatlakların zararı olarak geçmez; 'twice as expensive' bilgisi kendi kendini onaran betonun fiyatıyla ilgilidir.

questions.passage: When sociologists study social life in cities, they have traditionally focused on strong ties: relationships with family members and close friends. In recent years, however, attention has shifted to what are known as weak ties, the casual connections people form with acquaintances such as a neighbour met at the bus stop or the owner of a corner shop. Although such encounters may seem trivial, research suggests that they contribute considerably to well-being. In a two-year study of four districts in the city of Halvik, researchers found that residents who reported frequent brief interactions with acquaintances felt more attached to their neighbourhood and less lonely, regardless of how many close friends they had. Weak ties also appear to serve a practical function, as they are a common source of information about jobs, services and local events that close friends, who tend to move in the same circles, are unlikely to provide. The study's findings have implications for urban design. Districts with small independent shops, wide pavements and benches generated far more chance encounters than those dominated by large shopping centres and multi-lane roads. The authors caution, though, that physical design alone cannot create community: in one well-designed district, a high rate of residents moving in and out prevented acquaintances from forming. They conclude that stable housing is as important as attractive streets.
questions.text: The passage is mainly concerned with ----.
options: the reasons why city dwellers have fewer close friends and acquaintances than rural residents
the decline of small independent shops in modern cities
the methods sociologists use to measure loneliness
the value of casual relationships in urban life and the conditions that encourage them
the economic benefits of building large shopping centres
questions.explanation: Parça, tanıdıklarla kurulan zayıf bağların (weak ties) iyi oluşa katkısını ve bu bağları kolaylaştıran kentsel tasarım ile istikrarlı konut koşullarını ele alır; bu da gündelik ilişkilerin değeri ve onları destekleyen koşullardır. Kır-kent karşılaştırması yapılmaz; küçük dükkânlar yalnızca bir örnek olarak geçer; büyük alışveriş merkezlerinin ekonomik yararı ise hiç tartışılmaz.

questions.passage: When sociologists study social life in cities, they have traditionally focused on strong ties: relationships with family members and close friends. In recent years, however, attention has shifted to what are known as weak ties, the casual connections people form with acquaintances such as a neighbour met at the bus stop or the owner of a corner shop. Although such encounters may seem trivial, research suggests that they contribute considerably to well-being. In a two-year study of four districts in the city of Halvik, researchers found that residents who reported frequent brief interactions with acquaintances felt more attached to their neighbourhood and less lonely, regardless of how many close friends they had. Weak ties also appear to serve a practical function, as they are a common source of information about jobs, services and local events that close friends, who tend to move in the same circles, are unlikely to provide. The study's findings have implications for urban design. Districts with small independent shops, wide pavements and benches generated far more chance encounters than those dominated by large shopping centres and multi-lane roads. The authors caution, though, that physical design alone cannot create community: in one well-designed district, a high rate of residents moving in and out prevented acquaintances from forming. They conclude that stable housing is as important as attractive streets.

the streets were dominated by multi-lane roads

questions.passage: In English, a speaker can say 'It rained last night' without indicating how he or she knows this. In a number of the world's languages, however, such a statement would be grammatically incomplete. These languages have a feature known as evidentiality, which requires speakers to mark the source of their information. A verb might take one ending if the speaker saw the rain directly, another if they inferred it from wet streets, and yet another if someone else told them about it. Turkish offers a familiar example, distinguishing between forms such as 'geldi' and 'gelmiş', although some languages of the Amazon basin have far more elaborate systems with four or five categories. Researchers have long wondered whether such grammatical requirements shape the way speakers think. Some experimental studies suggest that children who grow up speaking an evidential language become aware of the sources of their knowledge earlier than other children, but the evidence remains mixed, and other studies have found no clear difference. What is less disputed is the social dimension of evidentiality. In communities where these systems are used, a speaker who reports second-hand information as if it had been witnessed may be regarded as dishonest or careless. Grammar, in such cases, becomes a tool for holding speakers accountable for what they say.

questions.passage: In many education systems, pupils are separated at some point into different types of school according to their academic performance. The age at which this happens varies widely: in some countries selection takes place as early as ten, while in others all pupils follow a common curriculum until sixteen. Supporters of early selection argue that it allows teaching to be matched more closely to pupils' abilities, benefiting both high achievers and those who struggle. Critics counter that decisions made at ten are unreliable and tend to reflect family background as much as talent. A reform introduced in the republic of Veloria in 2008 offers a rare opportunity to compare the two approaches. The government postponed selection from the age of ten to fifteen, but, for budgetary reasons, implemented the change in only half of its provinces at first. Researchers who compared the two groups of provinces over the following decade found that the reform reduced the gap in test scores between children from wealthy and poor families by almost a third. Importantly, the most able pupils did not perform worse under the new system, a finding that contradicted the main fear of the reform's opponents. However, the researchers stress that the reform was accompanied by substantial investment in teacher training, and that it is therefore difficult to attribute the improvements to the change in selection age alone.
questions.text: According to the passage, critics of early selection claim that ----.
options: it prevents high achievers from reaching their full potential
