questions.passage: Most people imagine earthquakes as sudden events in which the ground shakes violently for a few seconds. Over the past two decades, however, dense networks of GPS stations have revealed that faults can also release energy far more gently. In these so-called slow slip events, two blocks of crust slide past each other over days, weeks or even months, moving a few centimetres in total without producing any shaking that people can feel. Slow slip events have been detected along many subduction zones, where one tectonic plate sinks beneath another, and in some places they appear to recur at surprisingly regular intervals. Their significance for hazard assessment is still debated. On the one hand, by releasing accumulated strain, slow slips might reduce the likelihood of a large earthquake. On the other hand, they may transfer stress to neighbouring sections of a fault, bringing those sections closer to failure. A study of the Karsel subduction zone illustrates this ambiguity: of the eleven slow slip events recorded there between 2005 and 2020, two were followed within weeks by moderate earthquakes on adjacent segments, while the rest passed without incident. Seismologists hope that continued monitoring will eventually reveal which slow slips are harmless and which are warning signs, but they acknowledge that this goal may take decades to achieve.

options: they occur only far away from subduction zones

they are always followed by a large earthquake

Bu olaylar tam da dalma-batma (subduction) bölgelerinde saptanmıştır; toplam hareket yalnızca birkaç santimetredir; Karsel örneğinde çoğu olaydan sonra deprem olmadığı için 'always' yanlıştır.

questions.explanation: Ziyaretçinin 'derine indikçe daha eski zamana bakıyoruz' çıkarımı, rehberin bozulmamış kayada genç katmanların yaşlıların üstüne çöktüğünü söylemesine dayanır. Yerel halka sormak bilimsel bir yöntem değildir; kumtaşı ve kireçtaşı bilgisi, yıllık aşınma ve fosillerin azlığı ise katmanların konumu ile yaşı arasındaki ilişkiyi kurmaz.

questions.passage:
Mehmet: The council wants to turn the old car park into a public square.
Julia: I'm not sure that's wise. ----

questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Public squares make cities much more pleasant places to live in.
The car park was built in the 1970s, I believe.
I'd love to see more trees and benches there.
Our neighbourhood already has several popular cafés.
Many shop owners in the area depend on customers who arrive by car.
questions.explanation: Julia projeye kuşkuyla yaklaşır; Mehmet de yaya alanlarının yakındaki dükkânların işini artırdığını söyleyerek yanıt verir. Bu yüzden boşluğa, dükkân sahiplerinin arabayla gelen müşterilere bağımlı olduğu kaygısı gelir. Meydanların kenti güzelleştirdiği ya da daha fazla ağaç ve bank görmek istediği yönündeki sözler Julia'nın itirazıyla çelişir; otoparkın yapım yılı ise ilgisizdir.

questions.passage:
Student: Why are modern aircraft no longer made mainly of aluminium?

questions.explanation: Profesörün 'Exactly' diye onaylayıp daha hafif uçakların daha az yakıt yaktığını söylemesi, öğrencinin kompozitlerin aynı dayanımda alüminyumdan daha hafif olup olmadığını sorduğunu gösterir. Yolcu konforu, pilot eğitimi ve elektrik iletkenliği hafiflikle ilgili değildir; yakıt fiyatının düşüp düşmediği sorusu ise 'Exactly' yanıtıyla uyuşmaz.

questions.passage:
Zeynep: The ministry is planning to abolish homework in primary schools.

When did you finish your own homework?

questions.explanation: Zeynep'in 'görünüşe göre araştırmalar … gösteriyor' diyerek bir gerekçe sunması, Tom'un kararın nedenini sorduğunu gösterir. Ortaöğretim öğrencileri hakkındaki yorum konuyu değiştirir; bakanlığın daha fazla ödev vermesi gerektiği görüşü planla çelişir; Zeynep'in kendi ödevi ve okulların erken kapanması ise gelen yanıtla bağ kurmaz.

questions.passage:
Ali: Why do British and American people spell some words differently, like 'colour' and 'color'?
Professor Grant: ----

questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?

questions.explanation: Ali'nin farkların 'bilinçli olarak' getirildiği çıkarımı ve profesörün 'his reforms' ifadesi, boşlukta yazımı sadeleştirmek isteyen bir sözlük yazarından söz edildiğini gösterir. Konuşucu sayısı, öğrenenlerin anlama güçlüğü ve İngiltere içindeki telaffuz çeşitliliği bilinçli bir değişikliğe işaret etmez; iki yazımın da kabul edilmesi ise 'his' zamirine dayanak oluşturmaz.

questions.text:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

The new building regulations are so strict that few developers are willing to invest in the area.
options: Because the new building regulations are very strict, not many developers want to invest in the area.
Despite the strict new building regulations, many developers are eager to invest in the area.
Few developers invest in the area unless the building regulations are made stricter.
The building regulations became stricter after many developers had invested in the area.
If the building regulations were made stricter, developers would be less willing to invest in the area in future.
questions.explanation: 'So … that' yapısı neden-sonuç bildirir: Yönetmelikler çok katı olduğu için az sayıda yatırımcı bölgeye yatırım yapmak ister. 'Despite … many developers are eager' anlamı tersine çevirir; yönetmeliklerin daha katı hâle getirilmesini koşul yapan ya da gelecekteki bir katılaşmayı varsayan cümleler, kuralların zaten katı olduğu bilgisini değiştirir.

questions.text:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

It was not until the samples were examined under a microscope that the cracks in the alloy became apparent.
options: Although the samples were examined under a microscope, the cracks in the alloy went unnoticed.
The cracks in the alloy were noticed only when the samples were examined under a microscope.
The samples were examined under a microscope because the cracks in the alloy were clearly visible.
The alloy cracked as a result of being examined under a microscope.
Before the samples were examined under a microscope, the cracks in the alloy had already been repaired.
questions.explanation: 'It was not until … that' yapısı bir şeyin ancak belirli bir andan sonra gerçekleştiğini anlatır: Çatlaklar ancak örnekler mikroskopla incelenince fark edildi. 'Went unnoticed' anlamı tersine çevirir; çatlakların zaten açıkça görünür olduğunu söyleyen cümle 'not until' vurgusuyla çelişir; mikroskobun çatlamaya yol açması ya da çatlakların onarılması ise metinde yoktur.

questions.text:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

However nutritious a diet may be, it cannot compensate for a lack of physical activity.
options: A diet that is not nutritious enough can be balanced by plenty of physical activity.
Physical activity is only beneficial if it is combined with a nutritious diet.
No matter how nutritious a diet is, it cannot make up for insufficient physical activity.
Since this diet is nutritious, a lack of physical activity is not a serious problem.
The more nutritious a diet is, the less physical activity a person needs.
questions.explanation: 'However + sıfat' yapısı 'No matter how …' ile aynı anlamı verir; 'compensate for' da 'make up for' (telafi etmek) ile karşılanır. Yetersiz beslenmenin hareketle dengelenebileceği fikri yönü tersine çevirir; besleyici diyetin hareketsizliği önemsiz kıldığını ya da hareket gereksinimini azalttığını söyleyen cümleler asıl yargıyla çelişir.

questions.passage: For decades, dietary advice focused on individual nutrients, such as fat, sugar or salt. Nutrition researchers increasingly argue that this approach is too narrow, since people eat foods and meals rather than isolated nutrients. A growing body of evidence suggests that the degree to which food has been industrially processed may matter as much as its nutrient content. In one controlled trial, volunteers who were offered ultra-processed meals ate around 500 more calories a day than when they were offered minimally processed meals containing the same amounts of sugar, fat and fibre. ----
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Fat was therefore regarded as the main cause of heart disease in the 1960s.
Salt has been used to preserve food for thousands of years.
This suggests that processing itself, and not only nutrient composition, may influence how much people eat.
Volunteers in such trials are usually paid for their participation.
Most dietary fibre comes from whole grains, fruits and vegetables.
questions.explanation: Paragraf, besin içeriği aynı olan öğünlerden ultra işlenmiş olanın daha fazla yenmesini anlatan bir deneyle biter; bundan çıkan doğal sonuç, besin bileşimi kadar işlemenin de ne kadar yediğimizi etkileyebileceğidir. 1960'lardaki yağ görüşü ve tuzla saklama tarihi akışı geriye götürür; gönüllülerin ücreti ve lif kaynakları ise deneyin bulgusunu yorumlamaz.

questions.passage: ---- Below the surface, heat from deep within the planet warms underground water, which in some places reaches temperatures well above 150°C. questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?

Volcanic eruptions can cause enormous damage to surrounding communities.
Solar panels have become much cheaper over the past decade.
Most of the world's electricity is still produced by burning coal.

questions.explanation: Paragraf yerin altındaki ısının elektrik üretiminde kullanılmasını, avantajlarını ve sınırlılıklarını anlatır; bu yüzden jeotermal enerjiyi tanıtan cümle giriş için uygundur. Volkanik patlamaların zararları ve içme suyu olarak yeraltı suyu konuyu başka yöne çeker; güneş panellerinin ucuzlaması ve kömür ise jeotermal enerjiyi tanıtmaz.

questions.passage: Many countries are facing a growing shortage of qualified teachers. ---- Surveys of those who have left the profession frequently cite heavy workloads, limited opportunities for promotion and a feeling of being undervalued by society. Salary, interestingly, is often ranked below these factors. Policymakers who focus solely on pay rises may therefore be disappointed by the results.
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Student numbers at many universities have declined sharply since the 1990s.
Teachers in most countries are paid more than doctors and lawyers.
The problem stems not only from too few people entering teaching, but also from many experienced teachers leaving it early.
Online learning has made traditional classrooms unnecessary.
In the past, teaching was considered a suitable career mainly for women.
questions.explanation: Boşluktan sonra 'meslekten ayrılanlar' üzerine yapılan anketlerden söz edilir; bu yüzden boşluğa sorunun yalnızca mesleğe az kişinin girmesinden değil, deneyimli öğretmenlerin erken ayrılmasından da kaynaklandığını söyleyen cümle gelir. Üniversite öğrenci sayısı ve çevrim içi öğrenme konuyu değiştirir; öğretmen maaşlarının doktorlardan yüksek olduğu iddiası ise akışla ilgisizdir.

questions.passage: Cities are typically several degrees warmer than the surrounding countryside, a phenomenon known as the urban heat island effect. Concrete and asphalt absorb heat during the day and release it slowly at night, while the lack of vegetation reduces cooling through evaporation. ---- In response, several cities have begun painting roofs white, planting trees along streets and creating small parks on unused land.
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Rural areas, by contrast, are often home to a wider variety of wildlife.
The resulting heat poses serious health risks, particularly for elderly residents during summer heatwaves.
Asphalt was first used to pave roads in the nineteenth century.
Many people move to cities in search of better job opportunities.
Trees also provide shelter for birds and insects in winter.
questions.explanation: 'In response' ifadesi, önlemlerden önce bir sorunun dile getirilmesini gerektirir: Ortaya çıkan sıcaklık, özellikle yaz sıcak dalgalarında yaşlılar için ciddi sağlık riskleri doğurur. Kırsaldaki yaban hayatı ve asfaltın tarihi akışı keser; iş için kente göç ve ağaçların kuşlara barınak olması da kentlerin aldığı serinletme önlemlerini gerekçelendirmez.

questions.passage: (I) Glass appears to be a solid, but its atoms are arranged in a disordered pattern more typical of a liquid. Üçüncü cümle ise cam şişelerin Avrupa'da geri dönüşümüne geçerek atom yapısı ve dayanıklılık konusundan kopar; dördüncü cümledeki 'the same disordered arrangement' de doğrudan ikinci cümleye bağlanır.

Beşinci cümle ise işiten insanların seyahat için yabancı dil öğrenmesinden söz ederek işaret dilleri konusundan kopar; diğer cümleler aynı konuyu birbirine bağlı biçimde geliştirir.

questions.passage: (I) Iron deficiency is the most common nutritional deficiency in the world. (II) Vitamin D is produced in the skin when it is exposed to sunlight. İkinci cümle ise güneş ışığıyla deride D vitamini üretilmesine geçerek demir konusundan kopar; ayrıca üçüncü cümledeki 'It occurs when …' ifadesi birinci cümledeki demir eksikliğine gönderme yaptığı için araya giren cümle akışı bozar.

Dördüncü cümle ise merkezi ısıtma sistemlerinin teknik işleyişini açıklayarak konudan kopar; ikinci cümlede geçen 'central heating' yalnızca dairelerin bir özelliği olarak anılmıştır.

Birinci cümle ise üniversitelerin adayları ortaöğretim sınav sonuçlarına göre sıralamasından söz eder ve okul öncesi eğitimle hiçbir bağ kurmaz.

questions.text: The deep-sea expedition was forced to ---- its research programme after a storm severely damaged the vessel's sampling equipment.
options: endorse
curtail
replicate
assert
nurture
questions.explanation: Fırtınanın örnekleme ekipmanına ciddi zarar vermesi, araştırma programının 'curtail' (kısaltmak, kısıtlamak) edilmesini zorunlu kılar. 'Replicate' (tekrarlamak) ve 'endorse' (onaylamak, desteklemek) bu olumsuz durumla uyuşmaz; 'assert' (ileri sürmek) ve 'nurture' (beslemek, geliştirmek) de 'was forced to' ile anlamlı bir bağlam kurmaz.

questions.text: Some autoimmune diseases are notoriously difficult to diagnose because their early symptoms are ---- and easily mistaken for those of other conditions.
options: lucrative
punctual
ambiguous
meticulous
hostile
questions.explanation: Belirtilerin başka hastalıklarınkiyle kolayca karıştırılması, onların 'ambiguous' (belirsiz, birden çok yoruma açık) olmasıyla açıklanır. 'Lucrative' (kârlı), 'punctual' (dakik) ve 'meticulous' (titiz) belirtileri nitelemez; 'hostile' (düşmanca) ise teşhisin neden zor olduğunu açıklamaz.

questions.text: Employees who constantly feel that their efforts go unrecognised are far more likely to ---- and eventually leave the organisation.
options: show off
catch up
turn up
take over
burn out
questions.explanation: Emeklerinin sürekli görülmediğini hisseden çalışanların 'burn out' (tükenmek) ve sonunda kurumdan ayrılması mantıklı bir süreçtir. 'Show off' (gösteriş yapmak) ve 'catch up' (yetişmek) bu olumsuz durumla ilişkili değildir; 'turn up' (ortaya çıkmak, gelmek) ve 'take over' (devralmak) da ayrılıkla sonuçlanan bir süreci anlatmaz.

questions.text: The excavation ---- a wealth of everyday objects, from cooking pots to children's toys, which shed new light on domestic life in the settlement.
options: yielded
deprived
conceded
dismissed
abolished
questions.explanation: Kazının pişirme kaplarından oyuncaklara kadar pek çok gündelik nesne 'yielded' (ortaya çıkarmak, sağlamak) etmesi bağlamla tam uyumludur. 'Deprived' (yoksun bırakmak) ve 'abolished' (kaldırmak) nesnelerin bulunmasıyla çelişir; 'conceded' (kabul etmek) ve 'dismissed' (reddetmek) ise kazı için anlamsızdır.

questions.text: Farm incomes in the region are ---- dependent on a single crop, which leaves growers highly vulnerable to fluctuations in world prices.
options: barely
seldom
heavily
courteously
vividly
questions.explanation: Üreticilerin dünya fiyatlarındaki dalgalanmalara karşı savunmasız kalması, gelirlerin tek bir ürüne 'heavily' (büyük ölçüde) bağımlı olmasının sonucudur. 'Barely' (neredeyse hiç) ve 'seldom' (nadiren) bu savunmasızlıkla çelişir; 'courteously' (nazikçe) ve 'vividly' (canlı biçimde) ise 'dependent' sıfatını anlamlı biçimde nitelemez.

questions.text: Lithium-ion batteries, though efficient, raise concerns because the mining of their raw materials can be environmentally ----.
options: beneficial
negligible
compulsory
detrimental
spontaneous
questions.explanation: 'Raise concerns' (kaygı yaratmak) ifadesi, hammadde madenciliğinin çevre açısından 'detrimental' (zararlı) olabileceğini gösterir. 'Beneficial' (yararlı) ve 'negligible' (önemsiz) kaygının nedeni olamaz; 'compulsory' (zorunlu) ve 'spontaneous' (kendiliğinden) ise 'environmentally' ile anlamlı bir bütün oluşturmaz.

questions.text: Since the new storage facility opened last year, it ---- enough electricity to power about twenty thousand homes during peak hours.
options: has supplied
supplied
had supplied
was supplying
will supply
questions.explanation: 'Since + geçmiş zaman' yapısı geçmişte başlayıp günümüze uzanan bir durumu anlatır ve ana cümlede 'present perfect' gerektirir: 'has supplied'. 'Supplied' ve 'was supplying' süreci geçmişte bitmiş gösterir; 'had supplied' geçmişteki başka bir noktaya gönderme yapar; 'will supply' ise 'since' ile kullanılamaz.

questions.text: The immune system ---- distinguish between the body's own cells and foreign invaders; otherwise, it would attack healthy tissue.
options: could have
used to
would rather
need not
must be able to
questions.explanation: 'Otherwise, it would attack healthy tissue' ifadesi bir zorunluluk bildirir: Bağışıklık sistemi kendi hücreleriyle yabancıları ayırt edebilmek zorundadır, yani 'must be able to'. 'Need not' zorunluluğu ortadan kaldırarak anlamı bozar; 'used to' geçmişteki bir alışkanlığı anlatır; 'could have' yalın fiille kullanılamaz; 'would rather' ise tercih bildirir.

questions.text: Many of the clay tablets ---- at the site in the 1920s have still not been fully translated.

discovered

having discovered
to discover
questions.explanation: Cümlenin asıl fiili 'have still not been translated' olduğundan boşluğa 'tablets' sözcüğünü niteleyen kısaltılmış edilgen sıfat cümlesi gelir: 'discovered' (which were discovered). 'Were discovered' ikinci bir çekimli fiil oluşturarak cümleyi bozar; 'discovering' ve 'having discovered' etken anlam taşır, tabletler keşfeden değil keşfedilendir; 'to discover' ise amaç bildirir.

questions.text: The workers ---- the survey was conducted reported higher stress levels than the national average.
options: whom
which
among which
whose
among whom
questions.explanation: Anket işçilerin 'arasında' yapılmıştır ve 'workers' insan olduğu için edatlı yapı 'among whom' olmalıdır. 'Among which' insanlar için kullanılmaz; 'whom' ve 'which' tek başına kullanıldığında ardından gelen tam cümlede bir eksik öğe bulunmalıdır; 'whose' ise iyelik bildirir ve ardından bir isim ister.

questions.text: It is high time the government ---- measures to protect small farmers from the volatility of global markets.

has taken
will take
would have taken
took
questions.explanation: 'It is high time + özne' yapısından sonra fiil geçmiş zaman biçiminde gelir ve şimdiki bir gereklilik bildirir: 'took'. 'Takes', 'has taken' ve 'will take' bu kalıpla kullanılmaz; 'would have taken' ise gerçekleşmemiş bir geçmişi anlatarak kalıbın anlamını bozar.

questions.text: The new battery stores ---- energy as conventional models of the same size, yet it costs only slightly more.
options: three times as many
as three times much
three times as more
three times more as
three times as much
questions.explanation: 'Energy' sayılamayan bir isim olduğundan kat bildiren karşılaştırma 'three times as much … as' biçiminde kurulur. 'As many' sayılabilen isimlerle kullanılır; 'as three times much', 'three times as more' ve 'three times more as' ise sözcük sırası ya da karşılaştırma yapısı bakımından hatalıdır.

questions.text: ---- fever is unpleasant, it is in fact one of the body's ways of fighting infection, as many pathogens cannot multiply at higher temperatures.
options: Since

questions.passage: Inflammation is often thought of as something harmful, but it is in fact an essential part of the body's defence system. When tissue is injured or infected, immune cells release chemical signals that cause nearby blood vessels to widen, (1) ---- more blood and white cells to reach the affected area. This is (2) ---- inflamed skin becomes red, warm and swollen. Normally, the response switches off once the threat (3) ----. In some people, however, inflammation persists at a low level for months or years, even in the absence of infection. Such chronic inflammation has been linked to a wide range of conditions, (4) ---- heart disease, type 2 diabetes and certain cancers. Researchers are now investigating whether lifestyle factors such as diet, sleep and physical activity can help to (5) ---- this harmful form of inflammation.

questions.text: Although deep-sea mining could supply many of the metals needed for batteries, ----.

it was first proposed as long ago as the 1960s
since most of the ocean floor remains unexplored
it has therefore been encouraged by environmental groups
questions.explanation: 'Although' bir zıtlık ister: Derin deniz madenciliği batarya metallerini sağlayabilse de bilim insanları henüz iyi anlaşılmamış ekosistemleri yok edebileceği konusunda uyarır. Talebin artması ve 'therefore … encouraged' ifadesi zıtlık değil destek bildirir; 'since …' ana cümle içermez; 1960'lardaki öneri ise ilgisizdir.

'Had been produced' ve 'would have fought off' zaman uyumunu bozar; ateşin yaygın bir belirti olması ve doktorların yüzyıldır yaptığı araştırmalar ise koşulun sonucu değildir.

'Unless their employers trust them completely' doyumu güvensizliğe bağlayarak mantığı bozar; daha az ücret almak doyumu açıklamaz; 'So that' ve 'Whereas' ise anlamca uyumsuzdur.

'Than' 'no sooner' ile kullanılır, 'hardly' ile değil; 'until' ve 'so' bu kalıbı tamamlamaz; 'because they will uncover' ise zaman bakımından da hatalıdır.

questions.text: Farmers in the region have increasingly turned to drought-resistant crops, ----.

Aynı bilgiyi 'although' ile vermek zıtlık kurar ve mantığı bozar; 'so that the soil will become even drier' amaç olarak anlamsızdır; diğerleri zaman uyumunu bozar.

questions.text: While pumped hydroelectric storage remains the most widely used form of large-scale energy storage, ----.

Suyun yukarı pompalanması zıtlık değil açıklamadır; 'because …' ana cümle içermez; elektriğin gündüz tüketilmesi ilgisizdir; 'had been invented' ise zaman uyumunu bozar.

'As' ve 'because' neden bildirir ve 'so' kalıbını tamamlamaz; 'which' ve 'than' ise dil bilgisi açısından bu yapıya uymaz.

questions.text: Workers who take regular short breaks are often more productive than those who do not, ----.

Aynı bilgiyi 'even though' ile vermek zıtlık yaratır ve mantığı bozar; 'unless … had forbidden' zaman uyumsuzdur; molaların kısaltılması ve sektörlere göre ölçüm farkı ise ana fikri desteklemez.

questions.text: If global food prices continue to rise at the current rate, ----.

'Would have planted' üçüncü tip koşula aittir; 'was', 'had spent' ve 'introduced' ise geçmişteki olayları anlatır.

questions.text: Sea levels are rising not only because glaciers and ice sheets are melting; ----.

Buzulların büyümesi, seviyenin sabit kalması ve erimenin etkisiz olduğu iddiası ilk cümleyle çelişir; daha yüksek deniz duvarları ise bir neden değil, sonuca verilen bir tepkidir.

questions.passage: Every night, in one of the largest animal movements on the planet, billions of small fish, shrimp and other creatures rise hundreds of metres from the ocean depths towards the surface. They feed there under cover of darkness and then descend again before dawn. This daily vertical migration, as it is known, is thought to have evolved as a compromise: the surface waters are rich in food, but during the day they are also dangerous, since predators that hunt by sight can easily spot their prey. By retreating into the dim 'twilight zone' between 200 and 1,000 metres deep, the migrating animals reduce their risk of being eaten. The phenomenon was first noticed during the Second World War, when naval sonar operators detected a mysterious layer that seemed to rise and sink like a false sea floor. Today, scientists recognise that the migration matters far beyond the animals themselves. Because the creatures feed near the surface but release waste and are eaten at depth, they carry substantial quantities of carbon downwards every day. Some estimates suggest that the twilight zone may hold more fish by weight than the rest of the ocean combined, although such figures remain highly uncertain, as these animals are notoriously difficult to catch and count. The uncertainty has become pressing, since several countries are now considering commercial fishing in the twilight zone, a move that some researchers fear could weaken the ocean's ability to store carbon.

options: surface waters become too cold for small animals at night

predators that hunt by sight are most active at night
it helps the animals to escape from naval sonar

Besinin alacakaranlık bölgesinde daha bol olduğu ve yırtıcıların gece daha etkin olduğu metinle çelişir; sonar yalnızca keşfin aracıdır.

questions.passage: The immune system, like other parts of the body, changes with age. One of the most striking changes involves the thymus, a small organ behind the breastbone in which a type of white blood cell called the T cell matures. The thymus is largest in childhood and begins to shrink after puberty; by old age, much of it has been replaced by fat. As a result, older people produce far fewer new T cells and must rely increasingly on those generated earlier in life. This gradual decline helps to explain why elderly people are more vulnerable to infections and tend to respond less strongly to unfamiliar pathogens. Paradoxically, ageing is also associated with persistent, low-grade inflammation that can damage tissues even in the absence of infection. Scientists have not yet established why the system becomes both weaker and more inflammatory at the same time, although several explanations have been proposed, including the accumulation of damaged cells that release inflammatory signals. Encouragingly, the decline does not appear to be entirely fixed. In a small trial at the Brenholt Institute, older volunteers who followed a six-month programme of moderate exercise showed a measurable increase in their production of new T cells. The researchers stress, however, that the trial was too short and too small to show whether such changes actually protect people from disease.

Yaşlıların daha az T hücresine ihtiyaç duyduğu söylenmez, tersine enfeksiyonlara daha açıktırlar; kemik iliği ve daha az mikroba maruz kalma metinde geçmez; iltihabın hücreleri hemen yok ettiği de söylenmez.

questions.passage: Modern workplaces are full of interruptions: emails, messages, meetings and colleagues stopping by with quick questions. Many employees pride themselves on being able to handle several tasks at once, but research in work psychology suggests that this confidence may be misplaced. When people switch from one task to another, part of their attention tends to remain on the previous task, a phenomenon psychologists call attention residue. The effect is especially strong when the first task has been left unfinished. In one experiment at the Tamsin Business School, participants who were interrupted while solving a problem and then asked to evaluate a set of job applications made noticeably more errors in their evaluations than participants who had been allowed to finish the problem first. Interestingly, those who were given a moment to write down where they had stopped and what remained to be done performed almost as well as the uninterrupted group. The researchers suggest that this simple act of planning reassures the mind that the unfinished task will not be forgotten, thereby freeing attention for the new one. The findings have practical implications. Rather than attempting to eliminate interruptions altogether, which is rarely possible, organisations might encourage employees to pause briefly and record their progress before turning to something new.
questions.text: According to the passage, attention residue refers to ----.
options: the ability to handle several tasks at the same time without making errors or losing any time
the tendency for part of a person's attention to stay with a task they have just left
the errors people make when evaluating job applications
the time needed to read and reply to emails
the stress caused by an excessive number of meetings
questions.explanation: Parçada bir görevden diğerine geçildiğinde dikkatin bir bölümünün önceki görevde kalmasına 'attention residue' (dikkat kalıntısı) dendiği açıkça belirtilir. Birden fazla işi hatasız yürütme becerisi, metnin sorguladığı bir özgüvendir; iş başvurularındaki hatalar bu olgunun bir sonucudur, tanımı değildir; e-posta süresi ve toplantı stresi ise tanımla ilgisizdir.

questions.passage: As the share of electricity generated by wind and sun grows, so does the need for ways of storing surplus power until it is needed. Batteries dominate the market for short-term storage, but they degrade over time and depend on materials whose extraction raises environmental concerns. Some engineers are therefore returning to one of the simplest principles in physics: gravity. In a gravity storage system, surplus electricity is used to lift heavy weights, and the energy is recovered later by lowering them, which turns a generator. The idea is not new: pumped hydroelectric plants, which move water between two reservoirs at different heights, have operated on this principle for more than a century. What is new is the attempt to apply it in places without mountains or rivers. One promising option is to use disused mine shafts, which already provide the vertical distance the system requires. A pilot project in the former mining town of Grenvik, for example, suspends a 50-tonne weight in a shaft 500 metres deep. Its developers claim that the system can respond to changes in demand within a second and will operate for decades with little loss of capacity. Critics point out, however, that the amount of energy stored is modest compared with that of a pumped hydroelectric plant, and that the number of suitable shafts is limited. Gravity storage may thus serve as a useful supplement to existing technologies rather than a replacement for them.
questions.text: According to the passage, some engineers are interested in gravity storage partly because batteries ----.
options: cannot store electricity for even a few hours
are too heavy to be installed in mine shafts
were first developed more than a century ago
respond too slowly to sudden changes in demand, which makes them unsuitable for use in national grids
lose performance over time and rely on materials whose extraction may harm the environment

Bataryalar kısa süreli depolamada baskın olduğu için birkaç saat bile depolayamadıkları yanlıştır; bir asırdan uzun süredir çalışan teknoloji pompaj depolamalı santrallerdir; hızlı tepki ise Grenvik sistemi için söylenir.

questions.passage: Where did people in the past grow up, and how far did they travel during their lives? For a long time, archaeologists could answer such questions only indirectly, by studying the objects buried with the dead. A pot or brooch in a foreign style might suggest that its owner came from elsewhere, but it might equally indicate trade or changing fashions. Isotope analysis has made it possible to address the question more directly. As children's teeth form, they absorb chemical elements from the food and water consumed, including strontium, whose isotopic composition varies with the underlying geology. Because tooth enamel does not change after childhood, it preserves a chemical signature of the place where a person grew up. By comparing this signature with local values, researchers can identify individuals who were not born near where they were buried. At the cemetery of Aldmere, for instance, analysis of 60 skeletons showed that nearly a third of the adults had spent their childhood at least 100 kilometres away, a level of mobility far higher than the grave goods alone had suggested. Interestingly, most of the newcomers were women, which supports the view that marriage customs led women to move to their husbands' communities. Nevertheless, the method has limitations: regions with similar geology produce similar signatures, so a person's origin can often be narrowed down only to a range of possible areas.
questions.text: According to the passage, objects buried with the dead are an unreliable indicator of a person's origin because ----.
options: they may reflect trade or fashion rather than the owner's birthplace
they are usually too damaged to be identified
they were often added to graves centuries later
they absorb strontium from the surrounding soil
they were mostly made by women who had moved from elsewhere after marrying into the community
questions.explanation: Parçada yabancı tarzda bir çömlek ya da broşun sahibinin başka bir yerden geldiğini gösterebileceği, ama aynı şekilde ticarete ya da değişen modaya da işaret edebileceği belirtilir. Nesnelerin hasarlı olması ya da sonradan eklenmesi metinde geçmez; stronsiyumu emen dişlerdir, mezar eşyaları değil; kadınlar ise eşyaları yapanlar olarak değil göç edenler olarak anılır.

questions.passage:
Patient: I've had a cold three times this winter. Does that mean my immune system is weak?
Doctor: ----
Patient: That's a relief. So there's nothing I need to do?
Doctor: Just make sure you get enough sleep and wash your hands regularly.
questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Yes, you should start a course of antibiotics immediately.
You should have come to see me much earlier.
Not necessarily; most adults catch two to four colds a year, so that's quite normal.
Your blood pressure is slightly higher than it was last time.
I'm afraid we'll need to run several tests at the hospital to find out what is causing them.
questions.explanation: Hastanın 'That's a relief' (içim rahatladı) demesi, doktorun yetişkinlerin yılda iki ila dört kez soğuk algınlığı geçirmesinin normal olduğunu söyleyerek onu rahatlattığını gösterir. Hemen antibiyotik başlama önerisi ve birkaç test yapılması gerektiği hastayı rahatlatmaz; daha erken gelmesi gerektiği ve tansiyon bilgisi de bu tepkiye uymaz.

questions.passage:
Manager: Our staff survey shows that many employees feel exhausted, even though their working hours haven't increased.
HR specialist: ----
Manager: So it's not just how long they work, but how much control they have over their tasks?
HR specialist: Exactly. Giving them more say could make a big difference.
questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Research suggests that exhaustion is often linked to a lack of autonomy rather than to working time alone.
Then we should simply reduce their working hours.
Perhaps we need to hire more managers to supervise them closely and check on their progress every single day.
The survey was completed by over eighty per cent of the staff.
Many of them have been with the company for more than ten years.
questions.explanation: Yöneticinin 'sorun yalnızca ne kadar çalıştıkları değil, işleri üzerindeki denetimleri mi?' diye sonuç çıkarması, uzmanın tükenmişliği çalışma süresinden çok özerklik eksikliğine bağladığını gösterir. Çalışma saatlerini azaltma önerisi süreye odaklanır; daha sıkı denetim özerkliği azaltır; ankete katılım oranı ve kıdem ise bu çıkarıma zemin hazırlamaz.

questions.passage:
Leyla: I thought archaeologists always had to dig to find ancient sites.
Dr Moss: Not any more. ----
Leyla: So you can see buried walls without moving any soil?
Dr Moss: Yes, although we still excavate to confirm what the images show.
questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Most of our funding comes from private donors these days.
Digging is still the only reliable way to locate buried remains.
Many ancient sites have been destroyed by modern construction.
We usually work in summer, when the ground is dry.
Techniques such as ground-penetrating radar let us map structures beneath the surface.
questions.explanation: Leyla'nın toprağı kazmadan gömülü duvarların görülebildiği çıkarımı ve doktorun 'images' sözü, boşlukta yer altındaki yapıları haritalayan radar gibi tekniklerden söz edildiğini gösterir. Kazının hâlâ tek güvenilir yol olduğu 'Not any more' ile çelişir; özel bağışçılar, modern yapılaşmanın yıkımı ve yaz mevsimi ise Leyla'nın sorusunu açıklamaz.

questions.passage:
Farmer: The price of my wheat dropped by a third this year, even though my harvest was excellent.
Economist: ----
Farmer: So a good harvest everywhere actually hurts farmers like me?
Economist: In the short term, yes. That's why many farmers sign contracts that fix prices in advance.
questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: You should have planted a different crop instead of wheat.
Wheat is one of the oldest cultivated crops in the world.
That's because bumper harvests across the region increased supply, which pushed prices down.
Your harvest must have been damaged by the dry weather.
Prices usually rise when supply exceeds demand, so you should be earning more than ever this year.
questions.explanation: Çiftçinin 'her yerde iyi hasat aslında bizim gibi çiftçilere zarar mı veriyor?' çıkarımı, ekonomistin bölge genelindeki bol hasadın arzı artırıp fiyatları düşürdüğünü söylemesine dayanır. Arz talebi aşınca fiyatların yükseldiği iddiası ekonomik açıdan yanlıştır ve çıkarımla çelişir; hasadın kuraklıktan zarar gördüğü fikri 'excellent' ile çelişir; diğerleri ilgisizdir.

questions.passage:
Selin: Why can't we just store all the extra solar power from summer in batteries and use it in winter?
Engineer: ----
Selin: I see. So batteries are better for shifting power from day to night than from summer to winter?
Engineer: Exactly. Seasonal storage needs different solutions.
questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Solar panels produce much more electricity in summer than in winter.
Batteries are the cheapest way of storing energy for long periods, so we could easily keep summer power until winter.
We already store most of our winter electricity in batteries.
Batteries slowly lose their charge and would be far too expensive at the scale needed for months of storage.
Solar power is a clean and renewable source of energy.
questions.explanation: Selin'in bataryaların mevsimler arası değil gün içi kaydırma için daha uygun olduğu çıkarımı, mühendisin bataryaların zamanla şarj kaybettiğini ve aylarca depolama için çok pahalı olacağını söylemesine dayanır. Bataryaların uzun süreli depolamada en ucuz yol olduğu ya da kış elektriğinin zaten bataryalarda depolandığı bu çıkarımla çelişir; güneş enerjisine dair genel bilgiler ise soruyu yanıtlamaz.

questions.passage:
Tom: I read that the oceans absorb most of the extra heat caused by global warming.
Aylin: That's right, more than ninety per cent of it.
Tom: ----
Aylin: In a sense, yes. But warmer water also holds less oxygen, which is bad news for marine life.
questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: How deep is the ocean at its deepest point?
Why do oceans cover so much of the Earth's surface?
Isn't that good for us, since it keeps the air from warming even faster?
Shall we go swimming at the beach this weekend?
Who was the first person to measure the temperature of the sea?
questions.explanation: Aylin'in 'In a sense, yes. But …' (bir bakıma evet, ama …) diye yanıt vermesi, Tom'un okyanusların ısıyı emmesinin olumlu bir yanı olup olmadığını sorduğunu gösterir: Bu, havanın daha hızlı ısınmasını önlemez mi? Okyanusun derinliği ve yüzölçümü, hafta sonu yüzme planı ve ilk ölçümü yapan kişiye dair sorular 'evet, ama' yanıtıyla uyuşmaz.

questions.text:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

Scarcely had the crew lowered the instruments into the water when the storm forced them to abandon the survey.
options: The crew abandoned the survey before they had a chance to lower the instruments into the water.
As soon as the crew had lowered the instruments into the water, the storm forced them to give up the survey.
Although the storm was approaching, the crew lowered the instruments into the water and completed the survey as planned.
The crew lowered the instruments into the water only after the storm had passed.
The storm damaged the instruments, so the crew could hardly complete the survey.
questions.explanation: 'Scarcely had … when' yapısı iki olayın art arda geldiğini anlatır: Mürettebat aletleri suya indirir indirmez fırtına onları taramadan vazgeçirdi; bu anlamı 'As soon as' verir. Aletleri indiremeden vazgeçme sırayı bozar; taramayı tamamlama ve fırtına geçtikten sonra indirme anlamı tersine çevirir; aletlerin hasar görmesi ise cümlede yoktur.

questions.text:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

The more autonomy employees are given, the less likely they are to leave their jobs.

Giving employees more autonomy makes them more likely to look for new jobs.
Employees tend to stay in their jobs longer when they have greater autonomy.
Employees rarely leave their jobs, regardless of how much autonomy they have.
The less autonomy employees want, the longer they stay in their jobs.
questions.explanation: 'The more …, the less …' yapısı özerklik arttıkça işten ayrılma olasılığının azaldığını anlatır; bu, daha fazla özerkliği olan çalışanların işlerinde daha uzun kaldığı anlamına gelir. Far from being primitive, the farming methods used at the site appear to have been remarkably well adapted to the local climate.
options: The farming methods used at the site were primitive, but they were nevertheless surprisingly well adapted to the local climate.
Because the local climate was harsh, the farming methods used at the site remained primitive.
The farming methods used at the site were too advanced for the local climate.
Rather than being primitive, the farming methods used at the site seem to have suited the local climate extremely well.
It is unclear whether the farming methods used at the site were adapted to the local climate.
questions.explanation: 'Far from being primitive' (ilkel olmak bir yana) yöntemlerin ilkel olmadığını vurgular; 'appear to have been remarkably well adapted' da 'seem to have suited … extremely well' ile karşılanır. Yöntemlerin ilkel olduğunu kabul eden cümleler bu vurguyla çelişir; iklim için fazla gelişmiş olmaları ve uyumun belirsiz olduğu ise asıl cümlenin anlamını değiştirir.

questions.passage: In many developing countries, smallholder farmers sell their crops immediately after the harvest, when prices are at their lowest. They do so not because they are unaware that prices will rise later in the year, but because they need cash at once to repay debts and pay school fees. In an experiment conducted in several villages, farmers were offered small loans at harvest time on condition that they stored their grain for a few months. ----
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Grain prices on international markets are influenced by many different factors.
Those who accepted the loans sold their grain later at higher prices and increased their annual income considerably.
School fees have risen sharply in many rural areas over the past decade.
Most smallholders in these regions grow maize, rice or wheat.
Farmers in industrialised countries rarely sell their crops immediately after harvest, as they usually have access to large storage facilities.
questions.explanation: Paragraf hasat zamanı verilen küçük kredilerle ilgili bir deneyle biter; doğal sonraki adım deneyin sonucunu bildirmektir: Krediyi kabul edenler tahıllarını daha sonra yüksek fiyattan sattı ve gelirlerini artırdı. Uluslararası fiyat etkenleri, okul ücretlerindeki artış ve yetiştirilen ürünler akışı deneyin sonucuna bağlamaz; sanayileşmiş ülkelerle karşılaştırma ise konuyu değiştirir.

questions.passage: Why do we forget so much of what we learn? For much of the twentieth century, forgetting was viewed as a passive process in which memories simply faded with time. A growing body of research, however, suggests that sleep plays an active role in deciding which memories survive. During the deep stages of non-rapid eye movement sleep, the brain produces brief bursts of electrical activity known as sleep spindles. These bursts appear to coordinate the transfer of recently acquired information from the hippocampus, a region that stores memories temporarily, to the cortex, where they can be kept for years. In a study conducted at the fictional Halden Institute, volunteers learned pairs of words in the evening and were tested the following morning. Those whose recordings showed more spindles during the night recalled significantly more pairs, even after the researchers had accounted for differences in total sleep time. More intriguingly, when quiet sounds associated with particular word pairs were played to participants while they slept, those pairs were remembered better than others. The researchers caution, however, that the technique is far from a shortcut to effortless learning. The sounds only strengthened memories that had already been formed while the participants were awake, and they had no effect if played during lighter stages of sleep. Nevertheless, the results raise the possibility that sleep could one day be manipulated to help patients relearn skills lost after a stroke.

options: the reasons why people need less sleep as they grow older
the methods currently used to treat patients after a stroke
the negative effects of noise on the quality of sleep
how sleep contributes actively to strengthening certain memories

questions.explanation: Parça, unutmanın edilgen bir süreç sanıldığını, oysa uykunun hangi anıların kalıcı olacağına etkin biçimde karar verdiğini anlatır; bu nedenle ana konu uykunun bazı anıları güçlendirmedeki etkin rolüdür. İnme sonrası tedavi yalnızca son cümlede olasılık olarak geçer; gürültünün uykuya zararı ve yaşla azalan uyku ihtiyacı parçada yoktur.

A growing body of research, however, suggests that sleep plays an active role in deciding which memories survive. During the deep stages of non-rapid eye movement sleep, the brain produces brief bursts of electrical activity known as sleep spindles. These bursts appear to coordinate the transfer of recently acquired information from the hippocampus, a region that stores memories temporarily, to the cortex, where they can be kept for years. In a study conducted at the fictional Halden Institute, volunteers learned pairs of words in the evening and were tested the following morning. Those whose recordings showed more spindles during the night recalled significantly more pairs, even after the researchers had accounted for differences in total sleep time. More intriguingly, when quiet sounds associated with particular word pairs were played to participants while they slept, those pairs were remembered better than others. The researchers caution, however, that the technique is far from a shortcut to effortless learning. The sounds only strengthened memories that had already been formed while the participants were awake, and they had no effect if played during lighter stages of sleep. Nevertheless, the results raise the possibility that sleep could one day be manipulated to help patients relearn skills lost after a stroke.

questions.passage: Migration is often imagined as a single, decisive journey from one country to another. Historians and demographers increasingly reject this picture. Records from the fictional port of Merrowick, which kept detailed registers of departures and arrivals between 1850 and 1910, show that a large proportion of those who left eventually came back, some of them several times. Researchers who traced individual names through the registers estimate that nearly a third of emigrants returned within a decade. Many had never intended to settle abroad permanently; they left to earn money for a specific purpose, such as buying land or paying off a family debt, and went home once that goal had been achieved. This pattern, sometimes called circular migration, had consequences that extended far beyond the migrants themselves. Returnees brought back not only savings but also new farming techniques, political ideas and, in some cases, a reluctance to accept the authority of local landowners. Yet return was not always a sign of success. The registers suggest that a significant minority came back because of illness, unemployment or homesickness, and these individuals often found it difficult to reintegrate into communities that had changed in their absence. The researchers argue that national statistics, which typically counted only departures, have therefore exaggerated the scale of permanent emigration from the region.

options: reveal that many emigrants returned home, some of them more than once

questions.passage: In nature, colonies of ants and termites accomplish remarkable feats, from building elaborate nests to finding the shortest route to food, without any individual being in charge. Engineers have long hoped to reproduce this collective intelligence in machines. In swarm robotics, large numbers of simple and inexpensive robots follow a few basic rules, such as keeping a certain distance from their neighbours or moving towards a signal. Complex group behaviour then emerges from these local interactions rather than from instructions issued by a central controller. The approach offers obvious advantages. Because no single robot is essential, the swarm can continue to function even if many of its members fail, and it can be expanded simply by adding more units. A team at the fictional Tessaly Robotics Laboratory recently demonstrated a swarm of two hundred palm-sized robots that could jointly map the interior of a collapsed building, a task that would be dangerous for human rescuers. However, the same feature that makes swarms robust also makes them difficult to control. Since the behaviour of the group is not programmed directly, engineers cannot always predict how it will respond to unfamiliar situations, and small changes to individual rules can produce surprising results at the level of the swarm. Critics therefore argue that swarms should not be deployed where unexpected behaviour could put lives at risk until reliable methods of testing them have been developed.

questions.passage: Listeners in Western societies tend to describe music in minor keys as sad and music in major keys as happy. For a long time, many scholars assumed that this association was rooted in human biology. Some pointed out that sad speech is typically slower, quieter and lower in pitch, and that minor-key melodies share some of these acoustic features. If the link were purely biological, however, it should appear in all cultures. To test this idea, a team of musicologists from the fictional University of Corrin travelled to remote villages whose inhabitants had had little or no exposure to Western music. Participants listened to short melodies and were asked to point to a picture of either a smiling or a frowning face. Their responses were strikingly different from those of Western listeners: in several villages, minor-key melodies were as likely to be matched with smiling faces as major-key ones. By contrast, the tempo of a piece influenced judgements everywhere, with faster music consistently associated with happiness. The researchers concluded that the emotional meaning of major and minor keys is largely learned through cultural exposure, whereas the link between speed and mood may reflect something more universal. They acknowledge, however, that their sample was small and that even limited contact with radio or film soundtracks might have influenced some participants.
questions.text: The main purpose of the study described in the passage was to ----.
options: teach Western music to villagers who had never heard it before, using songs from popular films
measure how fast people in remote villages speak
find out whether the emotional meaning of major and minor keys is shared by all cultures
prove that sad speech is lower in pitch than happy speech
compare the popularity of different film soundtracks

Köylülere Batı müziği öğretmek ya da konuşma hızını ölçmek amaç değildir; hüzünlü konuşmanın özellikleri yalnızca arka plan bilgisidir.

questions.passage: In 2016 the fictional nation of Estmark became one of the first countries to set a minimum price for each unit of alcohol sold in shops. The policy was designed to target the cheapest, strongest drinks, which are disproportionately bought by heavy drinkers, while leaving the price of most beverages largely unchanged. Opponents argued that it would punish moderate drinkers on low incomes and do little to change the habits of those most at risk, who, they claimed, would simply cut back on food or other essentials. Five years later, an independent evaluation provided partial support for both sides. Overall alcohol sales fell by about three per cent, and the reduction was concentrated among households that had previously bought the most alcohol. Deaths directly attributable to alcohol declined by an estimated thirteen per cent, with the largest falls in the most deprived areas. However, the evaluation also found that a small group of people with severe alcohol dependence reported spending less on food and heating in order to maintain their drinking. The authors concluded that minimum pricing is an effective measure at the level of the population, but that it must be accompanied by improved access to treatment services for those whose drinking it cannot easily change.

options: increase the price of all alcoholic drinks by the same amount, regardless of their strength or type
raise the price of cheap, strong drinks without greatly affecting most other beverages
provide funding for alcohol treatment services
encourage moderate drinkers to choose stronger drinks
reduce the amount of food bought by heavy drinkers

Tüm içkilere aynı zammın yapıldığı yargısı bununla çelişir; tedavi hizmetleri değerlendirmenin önerisidir; ağır içicilerin yiyecek alımını azaltmak ise amaç değil eleştirilen bir yan etkidir.

questions.passage: In 2016 the fictional nation of Estmark became one of the first countries to set a minimum price for each unit of alcohol sold in shops. However, the evaluation also found that a small group of people with severe alcohol dependence reported spending less on food and heating in order to maintain their drinking. questions.passage: For more than a century, the Velan script, found on several hundred clay tablets excavated in the fictional valley of Ostrel, resisted every attempt at decipherment. The difficulty was not a shortage of material but the absence of any known starting point. Unlike some ancient scripts, which were eventually cracked thanks to inscriptions that repeated the same text in a known language, Velan offered no such key. Early scholars, convinced that the script must record an otherwise unknown language, tried to assign meanings to individual signs on the basis of their shapes, an approach that produced dozens of incompatible readings. The breakthrough came from an unexpected direction. A team of linguists and computer scientists analysed the frequency and position of every sign, discovering that certain combinations appeared almost exclusively at the beginning of tablets that also contained numerical signs. They proposed that these combinations represented place names, and when they tested this hypothesis against the names of towns recorded by a neighbouring civilisation, several matches emerged. These matches allowed the team to assign sound values to about a third of the signs, revealing that the language was, in fact, an early relative of one still spoken in the region today. Although many tablets remain only partly readable, the decipherment has already transformed historians' understanding of the valley's economy.
questions.text: According to the passage, the main obstacle to deciphering the Velan script was ----.
options: the small number of tablets that had been found in the valley so far

the lack of a bilingual text or any other known reference point

Tablet sayısının az olduğu yargısı 'not a shortage of material' ifadesiyle çelişir; tabletlerin kötü durumu ya da verilerin paylaşılmaması parçada geçmez.

questions.passage: Psychologists have long been interested in why some young children are able to resist an immediate temptation in order to obtain a larger reward later. In a well-known type of experiment, a child is offered one sweet now or two if they can wait alone in a room for fifteen minutes. Children who wait longer have often been described as having greater self-control, a trait that was thought to predict success later in life. More recent work, however, suggests that the decision to wait is not simply a matter of willpower. In a study at the fictional Brenna Child Research Centre, children first interacted with an adult who either kept or broke a promise to bring them better art materials. When later given the sweet test, children who had experienced the reliable adult waited, on average, four times longer than those who had been let down. From the child's point of view, the researchers argue, eating the sweet immediately is a rational choice if there is little reason to believe that the second one will ever arrive. The findings have important implications. Children growing up in unpredictable environments, where promises are frequently broken, may learn to take what is available rather than wait, and this behaviour should not automatically be interpreted as a lack of discipline.

questions.passage: Cities were once regarded by ecologists as biological deserts, places where nature had been replaced by concrete and that were therefore hardly worth studying. That view has changed dramatically. Researchers now recognise that urban areas create new environmental conditions, including higher temperatures, artificial light at night and unfamiliar food sources, and that many species are adapting to them, sometimes with surprising speed. A long-term study of a common songbird in the fictional city of Marlow found that urban populations had begun breeding nearly two weeks earlier than their rural relatives, probably because the city's warmer microclimate brings insects out earlier in spring. More remarkably, genetic analysis revealed small but consistent differences between the city and forest birds in genes linked to stress responses, suggesting that the change was not merely a matter of individuals adjusting their behaviour. Such findings have practical as well as theoretical value. If urban populations are evolving in distinct directions, conservation strategies designed for rural habitats may be poorly suited to cities. At the same time, some ecologists warn against exaggerating the trend. Most species cannot cope with urban conditions at all, and those that thrive tend to be generalists that were already widespread, so the overall effect of urbanisation on biodiversity remains strongly negative.

questions.passage: Cities were once regarded by ecologists as biological deserts, places where nature had been replaced by concrete and that were therefore hardly worth studying. That view has changed dramatically. Researchers now recognise that urban areas create new environmental conditions, including higher temperatures, artificial light at night and unfamiliar food sources, and that many species are adapting to them, sometimes with surprising speed. A long-term study of a common songbird in the fictional city of Marlow found that urban populations had begun breeding nearly two weeks earlier than their rural relatives, probably because the city's warmer microclimate brings insects out earlier in spring. More remarkably, genetic analysis revealed small but consistent differences between the city and forest birds in genes linked to stress responses, suggesting that the change was not merely a matter of individuals adjusting their behaviour. Such findings have practical as well as theoretical value. If urban populations are evolving in distinct directions, conservation strategies designed for rural habitats may be poorly suited to cities. At the same time, some ecologists warn against exaggerating the trend. Most species cannot cope with urban conditions at all, and those that thrive tend to be generalists that were already widespread, so the overall effect of urbanisation on biodiversity remains strongly negative.
questions.text: In the last part of the passage, some ecologists point out that ----.
options: generalist species are rarely found in cities
the evolution of urban species should be actively encouraged
urbanisation is still harmful to most species despite these adaptations
most species are eventually able to adapt to cities
rural habitats are less diverse than urban ones
questions.explanation: Bazı ekolojistler eğilimin abartılmaması gerektiğini, türlerin çoğunun kent koşullarıyla hiç baş edemediğini ve kentleşmenin biyolojik çeşitlilik üzerindeki genel etkisinin hâlâ güçlü biçimde olumsuz olduğunu vurgular. Türlerin çoğunun sonunda uyum sağlayabildiği yargısı bununla çelişir; kentte gelişenler zaten genelci türlerdir.

questions.passage: Standard economic models assume that people make consistent choices over time: if someone prefers a larger reward in a year to a smaller one in eleven months, they should also prefer the larger reward when the same choice is moved closer to the present. In practice, this is often not the case. Many people who would happily wait an extra month for a bigger payment in the distant future become far less patient when the smaller reward is available today. Economists call this tendency present bias, and it helps to explain why so many people postpone saving, exercising or giving up unhealthy habits. Interestingly, many people appear to be aware of their own weakness and, when offered the chance, voluntarily restrict their future options. In a field experiment with customers of a fictional rural bank, about a quarter of those offered a special savings account chose one that did not allow withdrawals until a date or amount they had set themselves, even though the account paid no extra interest. A year later, their savings had grown considerably more than those of a comparison group. Such commitment devices are not a universal solution, however. Some participants set targets so ambitious that they abandoned the account altogether, which suggests that the design of these tools matters as much as their availability.
questions.text: According to the passage, standard economic models assume that ----.
options: people always prefer smaller rewards that are available immediately, however long they must wait for larger ones
saving money is generally easier than exercising
people are unaware of their own weaknesses
people's preferences between two rewards do not change as the rewards come closer
banks should pay extra interest on long-term savings
questions.explanation: Standart modellere göre insanlar zaman içinde tutarlı seçimler yapar; büyük ödülü bir yıl sonra tercih eden kişi aynı seçim şimdiye yaklaştırıldığında da onu tercih etmelidir. Her zaman küçük ve anlık ödülü tercih etmek modellerin değil 'present bias' kavramının konusudur; diğer seçenekler modellerle ilgili değildir.

questions.passage: Doctors have long known that the same dose of a drug can have very different effects in different patients. Differences in age, body weight, kidney function and genes explain part of this variation, but a growing body of evidence points to another factor: the bacteria living in the gut. Many medicines taken by mouth pass through the intestine before entering the bloodstream, and along the way they encounter microbes equipped with a remarkable variety of enzymes. Some of these enzymes can chemically modify drugs, either inactivating them or, in certain cases, converting them into more potent or even toxic forms. In a laboratory study at the fictional Arden Institute, researchers exposed dozens of common medications to bacteria isolated from human volunteers and found that roughly two-thirds of the drugs were altered by at least one bacterial strain. Crucially, the strains responsible were present in some volunteers but absent in others. This could explain why a heart medication that works well for most patients is almost ineffective in a minority, whose gut bacteria appear to break it down before it can be absorbed. The researchers suggest that analysing a patient's microbiome before prescribing certain drugs could eventually become routine. They acknowledge, however, that laboratory conditions differ greatly from those inside the human body, and that clinical trials will be needed before any such practice is adopted.
questions.text: The passage is mainly about ----.
options: why kidney function determines the correct dose of a drug
the side effects of commonly prescribed heart medications in elderly patients and how to avoid them
methods of isolating bacteria from human volunteers
how gut bacteria may contribute to differences in the way patients respond to drugs
the history of drug development at the Arden Institute

Most children begin to speak in full sentences by the age of three.
Puzzles are therefore unsuitable for children under the age of five.
In their view, such private speech is a tool that helps children to organise their thinking and guide their actions.
Psychologists, too, regard it as a sign of confusion in most cases.
questions.explanation: 'Psychologists see it quite differently' ifadesinden sonra psikologların görüşü gelmelidir: Kendi kendine konuşma çocukların düşüncelerini düzenlemesine ve eylemlerini yönlendirmesine yardım eden bir araçtır; sonraki cümleler de bunu destekler. questions.passage: Most glaciers advance and retreat slowly, responding over decades to changes in snowfall and temperature. A small minority, however, behave in a strikingly different manner. These surge-type glaciers remain relatively stagnant for long periods, sometimes several decades, and then suddenly accelerate, flowing tens or even hundreds of times faster than usual for a few months or years before slowing down again. During a surge, the glacier front may advance several kilometres, blocking rivers and occasionally creating lakes that later drain catastrophically. For a long time, surges were regarded as a curiosity, since they appeared unrelated to climate: neighbouring glaciers exposed to identical conditions might behave in entirely different ways. Research over the past few decades has shifted attention from the surface to the bed of the glacier. During the quiet phase, ice accumulates in the upper reaches while the lower part thins, gradually steepening the glacier. Meanwhile, meltwater at the base is thought to become trapped in a poorly connected network of cavities, raising water pressure until the ice is partly lifted off its bed and friction falls dramatically. The surge ends when the drainage system reorganises into efficient channels that release the water, often in sudden floods at the glacier's snout. Because these processes depend on local geology, glaciologists caution that a surge should not be read as evidence that a glacier is healthy or growing.
questions.text: According to the passage, surge-type glaciers ----.
options: respond more quickly to changes in snowfall than other glaciers
are found only in regions where the climate has changed rapidly
flow at greatly increased speeds for a limited period after long phases of relative inactivity
continue to advance for several decades once a surge has begun, until the ice finally reaches the sea
always create lakes that eventually drain catastrophically
questions.explanation: Parçaya göre bu buzullar uzun süre durgun kalır, ardından birkaç ay ya da yıl boyunca olağandan onlarca, hatta yüzlerce kat hızlı akar: 'flow at greatly increased speeds for a limited period after long phases of relative inactivity'. Göller yalnızca 'occasionally' (zaman zaman) oluştuğu için 'always create lakes ...' yanlıştır; on yıllar süren olan hızlanma değil durgunluk evresidir.

questions.passage: Most glaciers advance and retreat slowly, responding over decades to changes in snowfall and temperature. A small minority, however, behave in a strikingly different manner. These surge-type glaciers remain relatively stagnant for long periods, sometimes several decades, and then suddenly accelerate, flowing tens or even hundreds of times faster than usual for a few months or years before slowing down again. During a surge, the glacier front may advance several kilometres, blocking rivers and occasionally creating lakes that later drain catastrophically. For a long time, surges were regarded as a curiosity, since they appeared unrelated to climate: neighbouring glaciers exposed to identical conditions might behave in entirely different ways. Research over the past few decades has shifted attention from the surface to the bed of the glacier. During the quiet phase, ice accumulates in the upper reaches while the lower part thins, gradually steepening the glacier. Meanwhile, meltwater at the base is thought to become trapped in a poorly connected network of cavities, raising water pressure until the ice is partly lifted off its bed and friction falls dramatically. The surge ends when the drainage system reorganises into efficient channels that release the water, often in sudden floods at the glacier's snout. Because these processes depend on local geology, glaciologists caution that a surge should not be read as evidence that a glacier is healthy or growing.
questions.text: In the last sentence, the author warns that ----.
options: surging glaciers are likely to disappear sooner than other glaciers
a glacier surge is not a reliable indicator of the glacier's overall condition
local geology is less important than climate in triggering surges, according to most glaciologists
glaciologists have exaggerated the danger posed by surges
surges prove that glaciers are growing in a warming climate
questions.explanation: Son cümle, hızlanmanın buzulun sağlıklı olduğunun ya da büyüdüğünün kanıtı sayılmaması gerektiğini söyler: 'a glacier surge is not a reliable indicator of the glacier's overall condition'. 'Surges prove that glaciers are growing ...' bu uyarının tam tersidir; 'local geology is less important than climate ...' ise süreçlerin yerel jeolojiye bağlı olduğu bilgisiyle çelişir.

questions.passage: Informed consent is often described as the cornerstone of ethical clinical research, yet a substantial body of evidence suggests that signing a consent form and genuinely understanding a study are not the same thing. One recurring problem has been labelled the 'therapeutic misconception': participants assume that every decision in a trial is made in their personal interest, as it would be in ordinary medical care. In reality, a trial is designed to answer a scientific question. Patients may be assigned to treatments by chance, doses may be fixed by protocol rather than adjusted to individual needs, and some procedures, such as additional biopsies, may be performed purely to collect data. Surveys of trial participants have repeatedly found that many could not explain randomisation or believed that their doctor had chosen the best treatment for them. Critics argue that the problem is aggravated by consent documents that have grown ever longer, partly because institutions draft them to protect themselves from legal liability rather than to inform. Some researchers have therefore experimented with shorter forms, structured conversations and simple comprehension quizzes. Early results indicate that such measures can improve understanding without reducing willingness to enrol, contradicting a widespread fear among investigators. Nonetheless, ethicists caution that no format can substitute for the time and attention of a researcher who is prepared to answer difficult questions honestly.
questions.text: The 'therapeutic misconception' mentioned in the passage refers to ----.
options: doctors' tendency to recommend experimental treatments over proven ones
the false assumption that clinical trials are always conducted for profit by large pharmaceutical companies
the refusal of patients to take part in randomised studies
researchers' belief that consent forms protect participants from harm
participants' mistaken belief that the procedures in a trial are chosen for their individual benefit
questions.explanation: Parçada bu kavram, katılımcıların çalışmadaki her kararın sıradan tıbbi bakımda olduğu gibi kendi çıkarları için alındığını sanması olarak tanımlanır: 'participants' mistaken belief that the procedures in a trial are chosen for their individual benefit'. Kâr amacı varsayımı ya da hastaların randomize çalışmaları reddetmesi parçada yer almaz.

questions.passage: Historians of medieval commerce have traditionally focused on the great maritime powers, but recent work on the so-called Pale Road of Marrowen, an overland route linking the northern port of Vardholm with the river markets of the interior, has drawn attention to the role of small inland towns. For nearly three centuries from about 1150, wagons carrying amber, furs and salted fish travelled south along this route, returning with cloth, wine and metalwork. Toll registers from the town of Orvesk, discovered in a monastery library only in 2009, show that traffic was far heavier than chroniclers had suggested: in some years more than four thousand wagons passed through its gates. Rather than simply taxing this traffic, Orvesk's council invested in it. It maintained bridges, regulated the quality of inns and, most strikingly, guaranteed compensation to merchants robbed within a day's journey of the town. This guarantee, funded by a small surcharge on every wagon, appears to have made the route considerably safer than rival paths through the forest. The decline of the Pale Road in the fifteenth century is usually attributed to the rise of sea routes, but the registers point to a more immediate cause: a series of disputes between Orvesk and its neighbours, which led each town to raise its tolls until merchants found the journey no longer worthwhile.
questions.text: The toll registers discovered in 2009 are important mainly because they ----.
options: prove that Orvesk was the largest town on the route
indicate that the route was used far more intensively than earlier accounts implied
show that amber was more valuable than cloth
reveal that chroniclers deliberately concealed the route's importance
contain the names of merchants who were robbed near Orvesk
questions.explanation: Kayıtlar, trafiğin vakanüvislerin belirttiğinden çok daha yoğun olduğunu ve bazı yıllarda dört binden fazla arabanın geçtiğini gösterir: 'indicate that the route was used far more intensively than earlier accounts implied'. Vakanüvislerin bilgiyi 'deliberately concealed' (kasten gizlediği) parçada söylenmez; Orvesk'in en büyük kasaba olduğu da belirtilmez.

questions.passage: When students are asked to judge whether a website is trustworthy, they typically do what generations of teachers have told them to do: they read the page carefully, examine its design, look for an 'About' section and check whether the author cites sources. A study comparing university students with professional fact-checkers, however, revealed that this careful, vertical reading is surprisingly ineffective. Polished design and an impressive list of references can be produced cheaply, and organisations promoting a particular agenda often present themselves in neutral, scholarly language. The fact-checkers behaved quite differently. Within seconds of landing on an unfamiliar site, they opened new browser tabs and searched for what independent sources said about the organisation behind it. This strategy, known as lateral reading, allowed them to identify questionable sites far more quickly and accurately than the students, many of whom spent several minutes on a page without ever discovering who had funded it. Paradoxically, the experts also read less of each page. Their skill lay not in deeper analysis of the content, but in knowing when to stop reading and look elsewhere. Researchers argue that such findings call for a change in how digital literacy is taught. Checklists that direct attention to features of the page itself may give learners a false sense of confidence, whereas brief, repeated practice in leaving a page to investigate its source appears to produce lasting improvements.
questions.text: According to the passage, vertical reading is ineffective because ----.
options: students rarely have enough time to read a whole page
fact-checkers have access to specialised tools and databases that students lack
most trustworthy websites do not include an 'About' section
the features it focuses on can easily be imitated by unreliable sources
it requires readers to open too many browser tabs
questions.explanation: Parçaya göre özenli tasarım, etkileyici kaynakça ve tarafsız akademik dil kolayca üretilebilir; bu yüzden dikey okumanın baktığı özellikler güvenilmez kaynaklarca taklit edilebilir: 'the features it focuses on can easily be imitated by unreliable sources'. Çok sayıda sekme açmak dikey değil yanal okumanın özelliğidir; zaman yetersizliğinden de söz edilmez.
